faq.question: Is this JPG to PNG converter really free?
faq.answer: Yes. There are no limits, watermarks, or hidden fees. All conversions run locally in your browser.

faq.question: Are my images uploaded to a server?
faq.answer: No. This tool uses your browser's Canvas API and Web Workers to convert images locally — your files never leave your device.

faq.question: Can I convert HEIC files from my iPhone?
faq.answer: Not in this tool — browsers can't decode HEIC directly. Use the HEIC to JPG converter first, then bring the result here if you need another format.

faq.question: Is there a limit on batch conversions?
faq.answer: No artificial limits are imposed — the only constraint is your device's available memory.

faq.question: Will converting JPG to PNG make the file larger?
faq.answer: Usually yes. PNG uses lossless compression, so a photo with lots of detail or gradients often becomes several times larger than the original JPG. If file size matters more than lossless quality, stick with JPG or try WebP instead.

faq.question: Does converting JPG to PNG add transparency?
faq.answer: No. JPG has no alpha channel, so the PNG output is fully opaque with no transparent pixels. To make parts of an image transparent you'd need a background remover tool first.

faq.question: What's the maximum image size this tool can handle?
faq.answer: It depends on your device's available memory, since conversion happens in your browser rather than on a server. Very large images (tens of megapixels) may slow down or fail on low-memory devices, but typical photos convert in a second or two.

faq.question: Can I convert multiple files at once?
faq.answer: Yes, select or drag in several images and each is converted to its own file; you can download them one by one or as a ZIP.

faq.question: Is my PDF data private?

faq.question: Are bookmarks, forms and links kept?

faq.question: Is there a size limit, and what is the file called?

faq.question: What happens if my JSON is invalid?
faq.answer: The status bar names the problem and shows its line and column, the editor underlines the spot, and clicking the message jumps the cursor there. If the problem is relaxed syntax such as comments or trailing commas, a Repair button fixes it.

faq.question: Does the tree view let me collapse and expand nested objects?

faq.question: Can it sort object keys alphabetically?

faq.question: Does it support JSON with comments or trailing commas?
faq.answer: The validator follows strict JSON, so it flags them — but one click on Repair removes comments and trailing commas, quotes bare property names, turns single quotes into double quotes and fixes Python-style True, False and None.

faq.question: What's the difference between beautify and minify here?
faq.answer: Format (beautify) adds indentation and line breaks for readability; Minify strips all unnecessary whitespace. Both keep very large numbers such as 12345678901234567890 exactly as written.

faq.question: Can I query the data with JSONPath?

faq.answer: Annual salary is divided by (hours per week × weeks per year) to determine the equivalent hourly rate.

faq.question: Does this account for taxes?
faq.answer: No, this calculates gross pay only. Consult a tax professional for net income estimates.

faq.question: Can I customize working hours?
faq.answer: Yes, you can adjust hours per week and paid weeks per year to match your schedule.

faq.question: How do you calculate daily and weekly rates?
faq.answer: Daily rate is your hourly rate multiplied by hours worked per day (derived from hours per week ÷ 5); weekly rate is hourly rate times hours per week.

faq.question: What if I work part-time?
faq.answer: Adjust the hours per week field to your actual schedule — the calculator recalculates all rates from that number.

faq.question: Does this account for overtime pay?

faq.question: Why does monthly pay not equal weekly pay times 4?
faq.answer: Monthly pay is annual salary divided by 12, not weekly pay times 4, since most months have slightly more than 4 weeks.

faq.question: Can I convert hourly pay to an annual salary?
faq.answer: Yes. Switch to I know my hourly rate, enter the rate and your weekly hours, and the annual, monthly, biweekly and weekly amounts are calculated, including overtime and unpaid weeks off.

faq.question: Does the converted JPG include the original photo's orientation?

faq.question: Can I convert Live Photos from my iPhone?

faq.question: Should I compress a PNG or a JPG for smaller file size?
faq.answer: JPG compression is lossy and generally shrinks photos much more than PNG, which is lossless — for photos, converting to JPG first typically saves more space than compressing a PNG.

faq.question: Does compressing an image multiple times keep degrading it?
faq.answer: Yes, since JPG compression is lossy, re-compressing an already-compressed JPG repeatedly will introduce additional quality loss each time.

faq.question: What's a good quality setting to use?
faq.answer: 70-85% is a common sweet spot that noticeably reduces file size while keeping visible quality loss minimal — lower it further if file size matters more than appearance.

faq.question: Why convert PNG to JPG?
faq.answer: JPG files are typically much smaller than PNG for photographic images, saving storage and bandwidth.

faq.question: What color fills in where my PNG was transparent?
faq.answer: White by default. Use the Background control to choose black, grey or any custom colour; transparent and semi-transparent pixels are blended onto it before saving.

faq.question: Will text or line art in my PNG look blurry as a JPG?
faq.answer: It can. JPG's compression is tuned for photographic gradients, and it tends to introduce soft artifacts around sharp edges like text or hard-edged graphics. For crisp graphics, PNG or WebP usually holds up better.

faq.question: Does converting to JPG remove the color profile from my PNG?
faq.answer: The conversion re-encodes pixel data through the canvas, which normalizes color to standard sRGB. If your PNG carried a wide-gamut or custom ICC profile, that specific profile isn't preserved in the JPG output.

faq.question: Why is my converted JPG file bigger than expected?
faq.answer: The quality slider defaults to 90%, which favors visual fidelity over file size. Lower the quality setting for a smaller file, or run the result through the image compressor for further savings.

faq.question: Does the PNG preserve gradients and filters from my SVG?

faq.question: Why does text in my SVG look different after converting to PNG?

howTo.text: Download the compressed PDF — the tool only offers it when it is actually smaller than your original.

faq.question: How much smaller will my PDF be?
faq.answer: It depends on the level and the content. Lossless usually saves little (often 0–20%). Balanced and Strong can shrink scanned or image-heavy PDFs dramatically, while text-only PDFs may not shrink at all because turning text into images can make them larger.

faq.question: Will compression affect quality?
faq.answer: Lossless does not change anything. Balanced (150 DPI) and Strong (100 DPI, lower JPEG quality) re-render every page as an image, so text becomes slightly softer.

faq.question: Why can't I select text after Balanced or Strong?
faq.answer: Those levels replace each page with a picture of the page, which is what makes the file small. Use Lossless if you need to keep selectable, searchable text.

faq.question: What if the result is bigger than my original?
faq.answer: The tool shows the size change and only offers a download when the file got smaller. Otherwise your original is the better file.

faq.question: Can I compress a password-protected PDF?
faq.answer: No, encrypted PDFs can't be opened by the compressor. Remove the password in the original application first — the tool will tell you if a file is protected.

faq.question: Why does a scanned PDF shrink so much more?
faq.answer: A scan is usually one large image per page at 300 DPI or more. Re-rendering at 150 or 100 DPI removes most of those pixels.

faq.question: Is my file uploaded anywhere, and why is a big file slow?
faq.answer: Nothing is uploaded — everything runs in your browser. Balanced and Strong render one page at a time, so long documents take longer; a progress counter shows where it is.

faq.answer: Yes. Chinese, Japanese, Thai and other languages written without spaces are split into words with your browser's built-in word segmenter, so word counts are close to what a dictionary-aware count gives. Character counts are always exact.

faq.question: Is there a limit to how much text I can paste in?
faq.answer: There's no hard cap enforced by the tool, but since counting runs live in your browser as you type, extremely large documents (tens of thousands of words) may make updates feel less instant.

faq.question: Does the character count include spaces?

faq.question: Can I count words in a specific selection instead of the whole text?
faq.answer: No, the counter currently tallies the entire contents of the text box rather than a highlighted selection. Paste only the portion you want counted if you need a partial count.

faq.question: Which character limits can I check?
faq.answer: Presets cover an X / Twitter post (280), SEO title (60), meta description (160), SMS (160), LinkedIn post (3,000) and Instagram caption (2,200), or you can enter your own limit. The bar turns amber near the limit and red once you go over.

faq.question: What is keyword density?
faq.answer: Keyword density is how often a word or phrase appears as a share of all words. Type one into the keyword box to see its count and percentage; for SEO a focus keyword is often used around 1–2% of the time.

faq.question: What is Base64 encoding used for?
faq.answer: Base64 encodes binary or text data into ASCII characters, commonly used for embedding data in URLs, JSON, or emails.

faq.answer: Yes. Text is converted with UTF-8, so emoji, accented letters and non-Latin scripts encode and decode correctly.

faq.question: Can I encode or decode files, not just text?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the file button to encode any file or image, and when decoded Base64 is not text the tool detects the file type, previews images and lets you download the file with the right extension.

faq.question: Why does decoding sometimes fail with an error?
faq.answer: Decoding fails if the input isn't valid Base64 — for example, it contains characters outside the Base64 alphabet or has incorrect padding.

faq.question: Does this support URL-safe Base64?
faq.answer: Yes. Tick URL-safe to use - and _ instead of + and /, and No padding to drop the = signs. Decoding accepts both standard and URL-safe Base64 automatically.

faq.question: Why does encoded text look longer than the original?
faq.answer: Base64 encodes every 3 bytes of input as 4 characters of output, so encoded text is roughly 33% larger than the original.

faq.question: Can it output a data: URI?
faq.answer: Yes. Tick As data: URI when encoding and the result is wrapped as data:<type>;base64,… ready to paste into HTML or CSS. Decoding accepts data: URIs as well.

faq.question: When do I need URL encoding?
faq.answer: URL encoding is needed when special characters (spaces, &, =, ?) appear in query parameters or path segments.

faq.question: What encoding standard does this use?
faq.answer: This uses the browser's native encodeURIComponent/decodeURIComponent functions (RFC 3986 percent-encoding).

faq.question: Is my data sent anywhere?
faq.answer: No, all encoding and decoding happens locally in your browser.

faq.question: What's the difference between encodeURIComponent and encodeURI?
faq.answer: Component mode (encodeURIComponent) encodes everything including / ? & = #, which is right for a single value. Full URL mode (encodeURI) keeps those characters so the URL still works. Form mode is Component with spaces written as +.

faq.question: How are spaces encoded?
faq.answer: As %20 in Component and Full URL modes, and as + in Form mode (application/x-www-form-urlencoded). Decoding in Form mode turns + back into a space.

faq.question: Can I encode an entire URL including the query string?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose Full URL mode, which keeps the characters that give a URL its structure (: / ? & = #) and only escapes unsafe ones. Component mode would escape those too, which is right for a single value but not a whole URL.

faq.question: Why does decoding fail on my input?
faq.answer: Decoding fails if the text contains a `%` not followed by two valid hex digits, which happens with malformed or already-partially-decoded input.

faq.question: Can it show the parts of a URL?
faq.answer: Yes. When the text is a full URL it is split into protocol, host, path, query and fragment, and every query parameter is listed with its decoded value.

faq.question: Does this tool verify the JWT signature?
faq.answer: Yes, when you ask it to. Enter the secret for HS256/384/512, or a public key (PEM or JWK) for RS, PS and ES algorithms, and press Verify. Until you do, the page clearly says the signature is not verified — decoding alone proves nothing.

faq.question: Is my token sent to a server?
faq.answer: No, decoding happens entirely locally in your browser using Base64URL decoding.

faq.question: What does the exp claim mean?
faq.answer: exp is a Unix timestamp for when the token expires. The tool shows it as a date with a live “in 2 hours” or “3 days ago” countdown.

faq.question: Can I use this to check if a token is expired?
faq.answer: Yes. The badges show Expired, Not valid yet (nbf) or Not expired. These only describe the time claims, not whether the token is genuine.

faq.question: What algorithm does the header show?
faq.answer: The decoded header includes the alg field, such as HS256 or RS256, indicating what algorithm the token was signed with — this is metadata only and isn't used to verify anything here.

faq.question: Can I decode a malformed or truncated JWT?
faq.answer: No. A signed JWT has three dot-separated Base64URL parts that decode to JSON; the tool tells you which part is wrong. Encrypted tokens (JWE, five parts) cannot be decoded here.

faq.question: Are custom claims in the payload displayed?
faq.answer: Yes, all claims in the payload are shown, both registered claims like iss and sub and any custom claims your application added.

faq.question: Are my tokens or keys stored anywhere?
faq.answer: No. Everything happens in your browser and, unlike most tools here, tokens and keys are never saved to your history.

faq.answer: This tool generates version 4 (random) UUIDs using the browser's native crypto.randomUUID API.

faq.question: Are the generated UUIDs guaranteed to be unique?
faq.answer: UUID v4 relies on 122 random bits, making collisions astronomically unlikely in practice, though no random generator can offer a mathematical uniqueness guarantee.

faq.question: Why do all UUIDs start with a similar pattern?
faq.answer: UUID v4 always has a fixed '4' in the version position and one of a few fixed bits in the variant position, so every UUID shares that structural pattern even though the rest is random.

faq.question: Which UUID version should I use?
faq.answer: Use v4 (random) for general identifiers. Use v7 for database keys, because it starts with a timestamp and sorts by creation time. v1 is timestamp-based and is mainly kept for compatibility.

faq.question: Can I check whether a UUID is valid?

faq.question: Why is MD5 labelled legacy?
faq.answer: MD5 and SHA-1 are cryptographically broken, so don't use them for security. They are included because many sites still publish MD5 or SHA-1 checksums for downloads.

faq.question: Is my file uploaded to a server?
faq.answer: No, hashing happens entirely locally using the Web Crypto API's SubtleCrypto.digest function.

faq.question: What is a hash used for?
faq.answer: Hashes are used to verify file integrity, detect duplicates, and create fixed-length fingerprints of data.

faq.question: Which hashing algorithms are available?
faq.answer: MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512 and CRC32. SHA uses your browser's Web Crypto API; MD5 and CRC32 are calculated by the tool itself.

faq.question: Can I hash a file instead of typed text?
faq.answer: Yes, drop a file and its checksum is computed from the file bytes locally. SHA hashing needs the whole file in memory, so files over 1 GB are limited to MD5 and CRC32.

faq.question: Why do two slightly different inputs produce completely different hashes?
faq.answer: This is the avalanche effect — cryptographic hash functions are designed so that even a one-character change produces a wholly different, unpredictable output.

faq.question: Can I use SHA-1 for security purposes?
faq.answer: No. SHA-1 is available for compatibility with older checksums, but collisions can be produced, so use SHA-256 or stronger.

faq.question: How do I check a downloaded file against its published checksum?
faq.answer: Drop the file, paste the published value in Compare with a checksum, and a green Match message appears if it equals any of the selected hashes. Hex and Base64 are both understood.

faq.answer: Multiply Y by (X divided by 100). For example, 20% of 150 is 150 × 0.20 = 30.

faq.question: How is percentage change calculated?

faq.answer: Yes, a negative result indicates a decrease from the original value.

faq.question: What's the difference between 'percentage of' and 'percentage change'?

faq.question: What can I put in the header and footer?

faq.question: How are pages split?
faq.answer: The document is measured first, and a new page starts only between paragraphs, table rows and list items, so lines and rows are never cut in half and a heading never ends a page. Only a single block taller than a page, such as a very long code block, can be split.

faq.question: Does it work with Arabic, Chinese, Japanese and other scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. Your browser draws the text, so any script your device has fonts for works in both PDF routes.

faq.question: Is my file uploaded anywhere?
faq.answer: No, everything happens in your browser. Long documents take longer because each page is rendered one at a time, and a progress counter shows where it is.

faq.question: Is my PDF uploaded anywhere?

faq.question: Can I combine pages from several PDFs?
faq.answer: Yes. Add as many PDFs as you like with Add PDF; every page joins the same grid, labelled with its file, and you can mix them in any order.

faq.question: How do I rotate or delete several pages at once?
faq.answer: Click pages to select them (a click toggles once something is selected), then use Left, Right, Delete or Duplicate. Select all and Clear selection help with big documents.

faq.question: What are the quick fixes for scanned documents?
faq.answer: Reverse all flips the whole order. Odd, then even groups pages 1, 3, 5… before 2, 4, 6…. Interleave duplex scan merges two scans — all front sides, then all back sides fed in reverse — into one correctly ordered document.

faq.question: Is there a page limit?

faq.question: Does it work with password-protected PDFs?

faq.question: What is the difference between a drawn and a digital signature?
faq.answer: A drawn signature is only a picture. A digital signature is a cryptographic seal made with your certificate's private key and stored inside the PDF. If anyone changes the file afterwards, readers such as Adobe Acrobat report that the signature is broken.

faq.question: Why does my reader say the signer is unverified?
faq.answer: A certificate created in this tool is self-signed, so the document is protected against edits but the reader cannot confirm who you are until its recipient trusts the certificate. faq.question: Is my document or signature uploaded?

faq.question: How do I get a clean signature from a photo?

faq.question: Why remove PDF metadata before sharing?
faq.answer: It can reveal the author's name, the software used and when the file was made — details you may not want to share. Download with all metadata removed gives you a clean copy.

faq.question: What is the XMP data option?
faq.answer: XMP is a second place where PDFs store properties, in XML form. Leaving Also remove XMP data ticked makes sure the old values don't survive there.

faq.question: Does it change the pages?

faq.question: Can I set the modified date to now?

faq.question: Is metadata the only thing that identifies the author?

exif-stripper.subheading: See the metadata hidden in your photos, then remove it losslessly — JPG, PNG and WebP — before sharing.

howTo.name: Upload your photos
howTo.text: Drag and drop one or more JPEG photos.

howTo.name: Review the metadata
howTo.text: See camera model, lens, date, ISO, and GPS coordinates found in each photo.

howTo.name: Strip and download
howTo.text: Click Strip & Download to get a clean copy with no metadata, or download all as a ZIP.

faq.question: What metadata gets removed?
faq.answer: EXIF (camera make and model, lens, capture date, ISO, GPS coordinates), XMP, IPTC / Photoshop data, comments and other embedded app data from JPG; text notes, EXIF and modification time from PNG; and EXIF and XMP from WebP. The tool lists what it removed for each file.

faq.question: Is my photo uploaded anywhere?
faq.answer: No. The file is read and rewritten entirely in your browser — nothing is sent to a server.

faq.question: Does stripping metadata reduce image quality?
faq.answer: No. The picture data is copied byte for byte and only the metadata is dropped, so there is no re-compression and no quality loss.

faq.question: Can I selectively remove just GPS data and keep other metadata?
faq.answer: Not field by field — metadata is removed as a whole. You can choose to keep the rotation flag (JPG) and the colour profile, which don't identify you.

faq.question: Which metadata fields are commonly found in phone photos?
faq.answer: Common fields include camera make and model, capture date and time, GPS coordinates, orientation, and sometimes the software used to edit the photo. Not every photo contains all of these.

faq.question: Does removing EXIF data affect how the photo displays or its orientation?
faq.answer: Rotation is stored in EXIF, so by default the tool keeps just the rotation flag for JPGs so a portrait photo doesn't turn sideways. Untick it to remove that too.

faq.question: Do I need to view the metadata before stripping it?
faq.answer: No, viewing the extracted fields is optional — you can strip metadata immediately without reviewing what's there first.

zero-width-remover.seoTitle: Zero-Width Space & Invisible Character Remover – Free Online
zero-width-remover.metaDescription: Find and remove zero-width spaces, bidi marks, soft hyphens, tag characters and other invisible Unicode, see exactly where they are, and keep emoji and Persian text intact. Free and private.
zero-width-remover.subheading: Find and remove invisible Unicode characters, see where they hide, and keep emoji and non-Latin text intact.

howTo.name: Paste your text
howTo.text: Paste text that may contain hidden or invisible characters.

howTo.name: Review what was found
howTo.text: See how many invisible characters were detected and where.

howTo.name: Copy the clean text
howTo.text: Copy the cleaned text with all invisible characters removed.

faq.question: Where do invisible characters come from?
faq.answer: They're often introduced accidentally when copying text from word processors, tracking links, or messaging apps.

faq.question: Which characters does this remove?
faq.answer: Zero-width spaces, no-break and word joiners, the BOM, soft hyphens, text-direction marks, invisible math operators, filler characters, Unicode tag characters and control characters. Unusual spaces such as the no-break space become a normal space. Each group has its own switch.

faq.question: Is my text sent anywhere?
faq.answer: No, cleaning happens entirely in your browser — nothing is uploaded.

faq.question: Does it detect characters I can't normally see in a text editor?
faq.answer: Yes. Reveal hidden shows every invisible character as a badge like ⟦U+200B⟧ in your text, and the Report tab lists each one with its position and name.

faq.question: Can it show me a count of how many invisible characters were found?
faq.answer: Yes, the tool reports exactly how many invisible characters were found and removed from your text.

faq.question: Will this remove legitimate formatting characters like non-breaking spaces?
faq.answer: Non-breaking and other unusual spaces are replaced with a normal space by default; untick that group to keep them. Zero-width joiners and variation selectors are kept by default because emoji and Persian, Arabic and Indic text depend on them.

faq.question: Why would invisible characters break my code or CMS content?
faq.answer: Zero-width characters can silently break string comparisons, search functionality, and copy-pasted code — since they're invisible, they're difficult to spot without a tool like this.

faq.question: Why are joiners kept by default?
faq.answer: The zero-width joiner builds emoji such as family and flag sequences, and the non-joiner is part of correct spelling in Persian and several other scripts. Removing them would break those texts, so you have to opt in.

hmac-generator.seoTitle: HMAC Generator Online – SHA-1/256/384/512, Free & Secure
hmac-generator.metaDescription: Generate an HMAC with SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512 as hex, Base64 or Base64URL, use a hex key, and verify a received signature. Computed locally in your browser.
hmac-generator.subheading: Generate an HMAC in hex or Base64 and verify a received signature, computed locally in your browser.

howTo.name: Enter your message
howTo.text: Type or paste the message you want to sign.

howTo.name: Enter your secret key
howTo.text: Type the secret key used to compute the HMAC.

howTo.name: Choose an algorithm
howTo.text: Select SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512.

howTo.name: Copy the HMAC
howTo.text: The resulting hex-encoded HMAC updates instantly — copy it with one click.

faq.question: How is the HMAC computed?
faq.answer: Using your browser's native Web Crypto API (crypto.subtle), which securely signs the message with your key using the selected hash algorithm.

faq.question: Is my secret key sent anywhere?
faq.answer: No, everything is computed locally in your browser — your key and message are never transmitted.

faq.question: What's the difference between HMAC and a plain hash?
faq.answer: A plain hash has no secret key, so anyone can compute it. An HMAC combines a secret key with the message, letting you verify both integrity and authenticity.

faq.question: Which hash algorithms can I use for the HMAC?
faq.answer: HMAC can be computed with SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512 as the underlying hash function, matching what's available in the Web Crypto API.

faq.question: Why would I use HMAC instead of just hashing the message?
faq.answer: A plain hash proves the message wasn't altered but anyone can compute it; HMAC also requires knowledge of a shared secret key, so it proves the message came from someone who holds that key.

faq.question: How do I verify a signature I received?
faq.answer: Paste the HMAC into Verify a signature (hex, Base64 or Base64URL). The tool compares it to the one it computes for your message and key and tells you whether they match.

faq.question: Can I use a hex or binary key?
faq.answer: Tick Key is hex to enter the key as pairs of hex digits instead of plain text.

json-to-typescript.seoTitle: JSON to TypeScript Converter – Interfaces & Zod Schemas, Free
json-to-typescript.metaDescription: Generate TypeScript interfaces, type aliases or Zod schemas from JSON in a full-screen editor. Detects optional fields and union types across array items. Free and private.
json-to-typescript.subheading: Generate TypeScript interfaces, type aliases and Zod schemas from JSON, with optional fields and unions detected for you.

howTo.name: Paste your JSON
howTo.text: Paste or type a JSON object or array in the editor.

howTo.name: Choose your options
howTo.text: Pick interface or type alias, toggle optional fields, and enable Zod schema generation if needed.

howTo.name: Copy or download
howTo.text: Copy the generated TypeScript code or download it as a .d.ts file.

faq.question: How are types inferred?
faq.answer: The tool walks your JSON structure and infers the corresponding TypeScript types — nested objects become their own interfaces, and arrays become typed lists.

faq.question: Does this require the Zod library?
faq.answer: No, the Zod schema is generated as plain text code for you to copy into a project that already has Zod installed — this tool has no dependency on it.

faq.question: Is my JSON uploaded anywhere?
faq.answer: No, type generation happens entirely in your browser.

faq.question: How does it handle arrays with mixed element types?
faq.answer: Items are merged into one type: numbers and strings become number | string, objects with different keys become one interface, and keys missing from some items are marked optional.

faq.question: Are optional and nullable fields detected?
faq.answer: Yes. A key missing from some objects in an array becomes optional (?), and a value that is sometimes null becomes a union such as string | null. Tick All optional to mark every field optional.

faq.question: Can I generate a type alias instead of an interface?
faq.answer: Yes, a toggle lets you switch between generating a TypeScript `interface` or a `type` alias.

faq.question: Does the Zod schema output include validation like min/max?
faq.answer: No — the schema reflects the shape only (types, optional, nullable, unions), plus an import line and an inferred type. Add .min(), .email() and similar rules yourself.

faq.question: Can I rename the root type or add export and readonly?
faq.answer: Yes. The toolbar sets the root type name and toggles export, readonly and all-optional.

json-to-yaml.seoTitle: JSON to YAML Converter Online – Free, Instant, Both Directions
json-to-yaml.metaDescription: Convert JSON to YAML and YAML to JSON in a full-screen editor. Handles anchors, aliases, multiline strings, comments and multiple documents, with exact error positions. Free and private.
json-to-yaml.subheading: Convert between JSON and YAML in a full-screen editor — anchors, multiline strings and multi-document files included.

howTo.text: Paste your JSON or YAML into the editor.

faq.question: Is this a full YAML implementation?
faq.answer: It uses a complete YAML 1.2 parser (the open-source `yaml` library), so nested structures, block and flow styles, multiline strings, anchors and aliases and multiple documents all convert correctly.

faq.question: Is my data uploaded anywhere?
faq.answer: No, conversion happens entirely in your browser.

faq.question: Can I convert complex nested structures?
faq.answer: Yes, both directions handle deeply nested objects and arrays of objects.

faq.question: How does it represent JSON null values in YAML?
faq.answer: JSON null values are written as the literal `null` in the YAML output, matching standard YAML convention.

faq.question: Are YAML anchors and aliases supported when converting back to JSON?
faq.answer: Yes. Aliases are expanded to their full values, and merge keys written as <<: *name are merged into the mapping.

faq.question: Does indentation matter when pasting YAML in?
faq.answer: Yes, YAML structure comes from indentation. If it is inconsistent the status bar shows the line and column of the problem so you can fix it.

faq.question: Can it round-trip YAML comments?
faq.answer: No. Comments are dropped when YAML is parsed, and JSON has no way to store them.

faq.question: What happens with a YAML file that has several documents?
faq.answer: Documents separated by --- are converted to a JSON array with one entry per document.

sql-formatter.seoTitle: SQL Formatter Online – Beautify & Minify SQL Queries, Free
sql-formatter.metaDescription: Format SQL for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, BigQuery, Snowflake and more, with keyword case, indent and comma-first options. Comments are kept; minify safely. Free and private.

faq.question: Which SQL dialects are supported?
faq.answer: Standard SQL, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, SQL Server (T-SQL), Oracle PL/SQL, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Spark, Hive, Trino, DB2, DuckDB and ClickHouse. Pick yours so quoting and keywords are understood.

faq.question: Does it validate my SQL?
faq.answer: It parses the query to format it, so serious syntax problems such as an unclosed bracket are reported with their line and column. It is not a full validator — it can't know your tables or columns.

faq.question: Is my query uploaded anywhere?
faq.answer: No, formatting happens entirely in your browser.

faq.question: Can I choose indentation style, like tabs vs spaces?
faq.answer: Yes: 2 spaces, 4 spaces or tabs.

faq.question: Does it uppercase SQL keywords automatically?
faq.answer: By default, but you can choose UPPER, lower or As typed.

faq.question: Can it format complex queries with subqueries and joins?
faq.answer: Yes, the formatter handles nested subqueries and multi-table joins, indenting each clause for readability.

faq.question: What happens if my SQL has a syntax error?
faq.answer: Formatting stops, the status bar shows the line and column, and the editor underlines the spot. Minify still works on any text.

faq.question: Are my comments kept?
faq.answer: Yes. Line comments (--) and block comments (/* */) are preserved when formatting. Minify removes them, but never touches string literals or quoted identifiers.

json-to-csv.seoTitle: JSON to CSV Converter Online – Free, Instant, No Upload
json-to-csv.metaDescription: Convert a JSON array to CSV with your choice of delimiter, flattened or JSON nested values, joined arrays, quote-all, Excel BOM and formula protection, plus a table preview. Free and private.
json-to-csv.subheading: Convert JSON to CSV with delimiter, nesting, arrays, Excel and formula-safety options, and a table preview.

howTo.name: Paste your JSON
howTo.text: Paste a JSON array of objects into the editor.

howTo.name: View the CSV output
howTo.text: See the converted CSV appear instantly, with columns from your object keys.

howTo.name: Copy or download
howTo.text: Copy the CSV text or download it as a .csv file.

faq.question: What JSON format works best?
faq.answer: An array of flat objects with consistent keys, e.g. [{"name": "A", "price": 10}, ...] — this maps cleanly to spreadsheet rows and columns.

faq.question: What happens with nested objects?
faq.answer: With Flatten objects on, nested keys become dotted columns such as team.name. Turn it off to keep nested values as JSON text in a single cell. Arrays are written as JSON, or joined with semicolons when you tick Join arrays.

faq.question: Is my data uploaded anywhere?
faq.answer: No, conversion happens entirely in your browser.

faq.question: Can I choose which fields get exported as columns?
faq.answer: Every key found in any object becomes a column. To drop some, delete them from the JSON first.

faq.question: How are commas or quotes inside values handled?
faq.answer: Values containing the delimiter, quotes, line breaks or leading and trailing spaces are wrapped in quotes with inner quotes doubled, following RFC 4180. Quote all forces quotes everywhere.

faq.question: Does column order match the order of keys in my JSON?
faq.answer: Columns follow the order in which keys first appear across the objects, so keep keys in a consistent order for predictable columns.

faq.question: Can I download the result directly as a .csv file?
faq.answer: Yes, a dedicated download button saves the converted output as a .csv file.

faq.question: Will Excel open the file correctly?
faq.answer: Tick Excel BOM to add a byte-order mark so accents display properly, choose Semicolon if your region uses it, and tick Formula guard to stop values starting with = + - or @ from being run as formulas.

code-minifier.seoTitle: HTML & CSS Minifier Online – Free, Instant, No Upload
code-minifier.metaDescription: Minify HTML, CSS, JavaScript, JSON and SVG in the browser and see exact size savings plus gzip size. Beautify CSS and JSON too. Free, private, no upload.
code-minifier.subheading: Minify HTML, CSS, JavaScript, JSON and SVG — with before/after size and gzip estimate, 100% local.

howTo.name: Paste or drop your code
howTo.text: Type, paste or open a file — the result updates as you go.

howTo.name: Check the savings
howTo.text: The status bar shows the size before and after, and an estimate of the gzip size.

howTo.name: Copy or download
howTo.text: Copy the result or download it as a file.

faq.question: Will minifying break my code?
faq.answer: The minifiers are careful: strings, url() values, <pre> and <textarea> content are left untouched, CSS selectors like `a :hover` keep their meaning, and calc() keeps its spaces. JavaScript uses the Terser minifier. Always test the result.

faq.question: How much size does minifying save?
faq.answer: It varies by how much whitespace and commenting your original code has — the tool shows an exact before/after size comparison.

faq.question: Is my code uploaded anywhere?
faq.answer: No, minification happens entirely in your browser.

faq.question: Does it minify JavaScript as well as HTML and CSS?
faq.answer: Yes. JavaScript is minified with Terser (compression and variable renaming), and JSON and SVG are supported too.

faq.question: Are HTML comments always removed?
faq.answer: They are removed by default, except IE conditional comments. Tick Keep comments to preserve them in HTML and CSS.

faq.question: Does minifying CSS remove unused rules?
faq.answer: No, CSS minification only removes comments and unnecessary whitespace/formatting — it doesn't analyze your HTML to detect and remove unused selectors.

faq.question: Can I reverse minification to get readable code back?
faq.answer: For CSS and JSON, tick Beautify instead to format them again. Minified HTML and JavaScript lose their original formatting, and JavaScript loses its variable names, so keep your source files.

faq.question: What does the gzip figure mean?
faq.answer: It is the size the minified text would be after gzip compression, which is what most servers send over the network, so it is closer to the real download size.

html-entity-encoder.seoTitle: HTML Entity Encoder / Decoder – Free, Instant, No Upload
html-entity-encoder.metaDescription: Encode text to HTML entities or decode entities back — named, decimal or hex, minimal or all characters — with a searchable entity reference. Free, private, no DOM tricks.
html-entity-encoder.subheading: Encode and decode HTML entities with named, decimal or hex styles and a searchable reference.

howTo.name: Choose encode or decode
howTo.text: Select whether you want to encode text or decode HTML entities.

howTo.name: Paste your text
howTo.text: Paste the text or HTML-entity-encoded string you want to convert.

howTo.name: Copy the result
howTo.text: Copy the encoded or decoded output to your clipboard.

faq.question: Why encode HTML entities?
faq.answer: To safely display special characters like <, >, and & as literal text inside HTML, without the browser interpreting them as markup.

faq.question: What entities can be decoded?
faq.answer: Named entities from the built-in table of about 250 common ones (such as ©, — and é), plus any decimal (©) or hex (©) numeric entity. Unknown names are left unchanged.

faq.question: Is my text uploaded anywhere?
faq.answer: No, encoding and decoding happen entirely in your browser.

faq.question: Does it encode all non-ASCII characters or just special ones?
faq.answer: You choose: only & < > " ', those plus every non-ASCII character, or every character. Non-ASCII characters use a named entity when one exists, otherwise a number.

faq.question: What's the difference between named and numeric entities?
faq.answer: Named entities like & are more readable, while numeric entities like & work for any Unicode code point, including ones without a defined name — this tool can output either.

faq.question: Why do I need to encode characters like & in HTML attributes?
faq.answer: Unencoded & or quote characters inside attribute values can break the HTML parser or be misread as marking the start of an entity, so encoding keeps the attribute value intact.

faq.question: Can decoding handle entities without a trailing semicolon?
faq.answer: No. Only well-formed entities that end in a semicolon are decoded, so text such as AT&T or &amp stays as typed.

faq.question: Is there a list of entities?
faq.answer: Yes. The Entity reference tab lists every entity the tool knows, searchable by name or by pasting the character, with a copy button for each.

title-case-converter.seoTitle: Title Case Converter – APA, Chicago, MLA & AP Style, Free
title-case-converter.metaDescription: Convert headlines to title case using AP, APA, Chicago/MLA or capitalize-every-word rules, keeping acronyms and brands like NASA and iPhone, line by line. Free and private.
title-case-converter.subheading: Capitalize headlines using AP, APA or Chicago / MLA rules — acronyms and brand names kept, one headline per line.

howTo.name: Paste your title
howTo.text: Type or paste the title or headline you want to capitalize.

howTo.name: Pick a style
howTo.text: Choose APA, Chicago, MLA, or AP style.

howTo.name: Copy the result
howTo.text: Copy the correctly capitalized title to your clipboard.

faq.question: What's the difference between the styles?
faq.answer: AP lowercases articles, conjunctions and prepositions of three letters or fewer. APA lowercases minor words of three letters or fewer. Chicago and MLA lowercase all prepositions, whatever their length. Every word capitalizes everything. Chicago and MLA agree on most titles, so they share one option.

faq.question: Is the first and last word always capitalized?
faq.answer: Yes. The first and last word, and the first word after a colon or dash, are always capitalized.

faq.question: Is my text uploaded anywhere?
faq.answer: No, capitalization happens entirely in your browser.

faq.question: How does it decide which small words to lowercase?
faq.answer: Each style has its own lists of minor words (articles, conjunctions and prepositions), shown in the style's tooltip. Everything else is capitalized.

faq.question: Does it handle hyphenated words correctly?
faq.answer: Yes. Each part of a hyphenated word is capitalized, so well-known becomes Well-Known.

faq.question: Can it capitalize titles with subtitles separated by a colon?
faq.answer: Yes, text is processed as a continuous string, so both the title and subtitle portions get title-cased consistently.

faq.question: Does it preserve intentional stylized capitalization, like brand names?
faq.answer: Yes, by default. Words that are all caps (NASA) or have inner capitals (iPhone, eBay) are left as they are. Untick Keep acronyms & brands to reformat them too.

url-slug-generator.seoTitle: URL Slug Generator Online – SEO-Friendly, Free & Instant
url-slug-generator.metaDescription: Turn titles into clean URL slugs with transliteration of accents, Cyrillic, Greek and Arabic, optional Unicode slugs, stop-word removal, max length and bulk conversion. Free and private.
url-slug-generator.subheading: Turn titles into clean, SEO-friendly URL slugs — transliteration, stop words, max length and bulk conversion.

howTo.name: Enter your title
howTo.text: Type or paste a blog post title or any text.

howTo.name: Adjust the options
howTo.text: Set a maximum length and choose hyphen or underscore as the separator.

howTo.name: Copy the slug
howTo.text: The URL-ready slug updates instantly — copy it with one click.

faq.question: How are accented characters handled?
faq.answer: They are transliterated to plain letters: é becomes e, ß becomes ss, æ becomes ae, and Cyrillic, Greek and Arabic letters become their Latin equivalents. Tick Keep non-Latin letters to keep letters from any script instead.

faq.question: What happens to special characters and spaces?
faq.answer: They're replaced with your chosen separator, and multiple consecutive separators are collapsed into one.

faq.question: Is my text uploaded anywhere?
faq.answer: No, slug generation happens entirely in your browser.

faq.question: Does it enforce a maximum slug length?
faq.answer: Optionally. Set Max length and the slug is cut at a whole word where possible. Leave it empty for no limit.

faq.question: Can I choose hyphens or underscores as the separator?
faq.answer: Yes: hyphen, underscore, dot or none.

faq.question: Does it remove stop words like 'a' or 'the'?
faq.answer: Optionally. Tick Drop stop words to remove common words such as a, the, of and and (a slug never ends up empty because of it).

faq.question: What happens to numbers in the title?
faq.answer: Numbers are kept as they are. Symbols such as & and % are turned into words (and, percent).

faq.question: Can I make many slugs at once?
faq.answer: Yes. Put one title per line and every line gets its own slug. A prefix such as https://site.com/blog can be added to each one.

faq.question: What about languages like Chinese or Japanese?
faq.answer: They cannot be transliterated reliably, so those characters would be dropped. Tick Keep non-Latin letters to keep them — modern browsers and search engines handle Unicode URLs.

opengraph-generator.seoTitle: OpenGraph & Meta Tag Generator – Live Preview, Free
opengraph-generator.metaDescription: Generate Open Graph and Twitter Card meta tags with live Google, X, Facebook, LinkedIn and Slack previews, length counters, image checks and a Next.js metadata export. Free and private.
opengraph-generator.subheading: Generate social share meta tags with live previews for Google, X, Facebook, LinkedIn and Slack, plus length counters and image checks.

howTo.name: Copy the code
howTo.text: Copy ready-to-paste HTML meta tags or a Next.js metadata object.

faq.question: What are OpenGraph tags used for?
faq.answer: They control how your page appears when shared on social media and messaging apps — the title, description, and preview image.

faq.question: Does this work with Next.js?
faq.answer: Yes. A ready-to-paste Next.js metadata export is generated next to the plain HTML tags, with all values safely escaped.

faq.question: Is my data uploaded anywhere?
faq.answer: No, the previews and generated code are built entirely in your browser.

faq.question: What image dimensions should I use for the OpenGraph image?
faq.answer: 1200×630 pixels is the widely recommended size for OpenGraph images, giving a good display across Facebook, LinkedIn, and most other platforms.

faq.question: Does this generate Twitter Card tags too?
faq.answer: Yes. It writes twitter:card (large image or summary), title, description, image, alt text, site and creator.

faq.question: Can I preview how the link looks on different platforms?
faq.answer: Yes. Tabs show Google search, X / Twitter (large or small card), Facebook / LinkedIn and Slack / Discord previews. Real rendering can differ slightly by platform.

faq.question: Why isn't my site showing the updated preview after I changed the tags?
faq.answer: Social platforms cache link previews — you'll typically need to use that platform's own debugging/cache-refresh tool (like Facebook's Sharing Debugger) to force it to re-read your updated tags.

faq.question: Are my values escaped in the output?
faq.answer: Yes. Quotes, ampersands and angle brackets are escaped in the HTML tags, and quotes and backslashes in the Next.js code, so the output can't break your markup. Tags with no value are left out.

duplicate-line-remover.seoTitle: Duplicate Line Remover & List Sorter – Free, Instant
duplicate-line-remover.metaDescription: Remove duplicate lines, show only duplicates or unique lines, count occurrences, and sort naturally, by length, reversed or shuffled — with live stats. Free and private.
duplicate-line-remover.subheading: Remove duplicate lines, find duplicates, count occurrences and sort — with live statistics.

howTo.name: Sort and copy
howTo.text: Pick a sort order, then copy the cleaned list.

faq.question: Which line is kept when duplicates are found?
faq.answer: The first occurrence is kept, with its original casing preserved even in case-insensitive mode.

faq.question: Can I sort without removing duplicates?
faq.answer: Yes, sorting and deduplication are independent options — use either one alone or together.

faq.question: Is my list uploaded anywhere?
faq.answer: No, everything is processed entirely in your browser.

faq.question: Is duplicate detection case-sensitive?
faq.answer: Not by default: Ignore case is on. Untick it to treat Apple and apple as different lines. The first occurrence keeps its original casing.

faq.question: Does it ignore leading or trailing whitespace when comparing lines?
faq.answer: Yes, when Trim spaces is on, lines that differ only in surrounding spaces count as the same.

faq.question: What sorting options are available besides alphabetical?
faq.answer: A to Z, Z to A, natural (item2 before item10), natural descending, shortest first, longest first, reverse order and shuffle.

faq.question: Can I remove blank lines at the same time?
faq.answer: Yes. Drop empty lines works alongside the other options, and the status bar reports how many were removed.

faq.question: Can I see only the duplicates, or count them?
faq.answer: Yes. Mode lets you show only lines that appear more than once, keep only lines that appear exactly once, or list each line with how many times it occurs.

svg-optimizer.seoTitle: SVG Optimizer Online – Free, Instant, No Upload

faq.question: Will optimizing change how my SVG looks?
faq.answer: No, all optimizations are visually lossless — only redundant markup like comments, unused IDs, and excess decimal precision are removed.

faq.question: What does 'clean unused IDs' do?
faq.answer: It scans the SVG for id attributes that are never referenced elsewhere (via url(#id) or href) and removes them, since unreferenced IDs add size with no purpose.

faq.question: Is my SVG uploaded anywhere?
faq.answer: No, optimization happens entirely in your browser.

faq.question: What specific things does the optimizer clean up?
faq.answer: It removes comments, strips metadata/title/description elements, cleans up unused ID attributes, and rounds numeric precision in path and shape coordinates — it doesn't simplify path geometry itself.

faq.question: Will optimizing break animations or JavaScript that references my SVG's IDs?
faq.answer: IDs that are actually referenced (via url() or href) are preserved — only genuinely unused IDs are removed, but double-check any external JavaScript that references IDs indirectly.

faq.question: How much smaller does an SVG typically get after optimizing?
faq.answer: This varies widely depending on how much unnecessary markup, comments, and excess decimal precision the original file contains — hand-exported SVGs from design tools often shrink noticeably more than already-clean ones.

faq.question: Can I paste raw SVG markup instead of uploading a file?
faq.answer: Yes, you can either paste SVG code directly into the text area or upload an .svg file.

wcag-contrast-checker.seoTitle: WCAG Color Contrast Checker – Free, Accurate, Instant
wcag-contrast-checker.metaDescription: Check whether your text and background colors meet WCAG AA and AAA accessibility contrast requirements — processed 100% locally in your browser.
wcag-contrast-checker.subheading: Check whether your text and background colors meet WCAG accessibility contrast requirements.

howTo.name: Pick your colors
howTo.text: Choose or type a foreground (text) color and a background color.

howTo.name: Check the ratio
howTo.text: See the exact contrast ratio and whether it passes AA and AAA thresholds.

howTo.name: Preview legibility
howTo.text: See live sample text rendered in your chosen colors at normal and large sizes.

faq.question: How is the contrast ratio calculated?
faq.answer: Using the official WCAG 2.x relative luminance formula, which gamma-corrects each color channel before weighting it by human luminance perception.

faq.question: What's the difference between AA and AAA?
faq.answer: AA is the standard accessibility requirement (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text); AAA is a stricter enhanced requirement (7:1 and 4.5:1 respectively).

faq.question: What counts as 'large text'?
faq.answer: Text that's 18pt or larger, or 14pt and bold, qualifies for the more lenient large-text thresholds.

faq.question: Does this tool check contrast for UI elements, not just text?
faq.answer: No, it checks the four standard text-contrast thresholds (AA and AAA, normal and large text) only — it doesn't check the separate 3:1 ratio WCAG requires for non-text UI components and graphical objects.

faq.question: Can I enter colors as HEX, RGB, or color names?
faq.answer: Most versions accept HEX codes and RGB values directly; check the input field for which formats are supported before typing in a color name.

faq.question: Why did my colors pass AA but fail AAA?
faq.answer: AAA requires a stricter 7:1 ratio for normal text compared to AA's 4.5:1, so a color pair with moderate contrast can satisfy the more lenient AA standard while falling short of AAA.

faq.question: What's the difference between AA and AAA compliance?
faq.answer: AA is the standard minimum most sites aim for (4.5:1 for normal text); AAA is a stricter, optional level (7:1) recommended for content aimed at users with low vision.

aspect-ratio-calculator.seoTitle: Aspect Ratio Calculator Online – Free & Instant
aspect-ratio-calculator.metaDescription: Calculate a scaled width or height that preserves your image or video's aspect ratio, with common ratio presets — instantly in your browser.

faq.question: How is the simplified ratio calculated?
faq.answer: The width and height are divided by their greatest common divisor (GCD) to produce the simplest whole-number ratio, like 1920×1080 simplifying to 16:9.

faq.question: Can I scale by height instead of width?
faq.answer: Yes, entering a target height calculates the matching width, and vice versa — only one is editable at a time to keep the ratio locked.

faq.question: Is my data uploaded anywhere?
faq.answer: No, all calculations happen entirely in your browser.

faq.question: What does the simplified ratio (e.g. 16:9) mean?
faq.answer: It's your width and height reduced to the smallest whole numbers that keep the same proportion, using their greatest common divisor.

faq.question: Can I lock the ratio and enter a target width to find the height?
faq.answer: Yes, entering either dimension automatically scales the other to preserve the original aspect ratio.

faq.question: Is this useful for video and screen resolutions too?
faq.answer: Yes, it works for any width/height pair — video frames, monitor resolutions, print dimensions, and image crops all use the same ratio math.

faq.question: What's the difference between aspect ratio and resolution?
faq.answer: Resolution is the exact pixel dimensions (e.g. 1920×1080); aspect ratio is the proportional relationship between width and height (e.g. 16:9), which many different resolutions can share.

faq.question: Why is there a maximum recording duration?
faq.answer: Animated GIFs store every frame uncompressed relative to video codecs, so file size and encoding time grow quickly — capping duration keeps exports fast and manageable.

faq.question: Why does a lower frame rate produce a smaller file?
faq.answer: Fewer frames means less data to encode and store, at the cost of smoother motion — 8–10 fps is a good balance for most screen recordings.

faq.question: Can I trim the recording before exporting as GIF?

faq.question: Can I loop the GIF or does it play once?
faq.answer: Animated GIFs loop by default in virtually all browsers and apps that display them, so your exported file will replay automatically without any extra setting needed.

faq.question: Why does my GIF look like it has fewer colors than my screen?
faq.answer: The GIF format is limited to a palette of 256 colors per frame, so smooth gradients or photo-like content can show visible banding compared to the original screen recording.

faq.question: Does the recording include my microphone audio?
