faq.question: Does duplicate name text affect the odds?
faq.answer: Yes, if a name appears multiple times in your list, it effectively has a higher chance of being picked, similar to extra raffle tickets.

faq.question: Are my names stored anywhere?
faq.answer: No, everything happens locally in your browser tab — nothing is uploaded or transmitted.

faq.question: Can I save multiple picks over time?
faq.answer: Yes, each time you click Save, that pick is added as a new entry to your local history, which you can review or restore from later.

random-number-generator.seoTitle: Random Number Generator – Custom Range, Instant Results
random-number-generator.metaDescription: Generate one or many random numbers in any range, with or without duplicates — free, instant, and 100% private.
random-number-generator.subheading: Generate random numbers within any range you choose — instantly and privately.

howTo.name: Set your range
howTo.text: Enter a minimum and maximum value.

howTo.name: Choose how many numbers
howTo.text: Set how many random numbers to generate at once.

howTo.name: Generate
howTo.text: Click Generate to produce your random number(s).

howTo.name: Copy the result
howTo.text: Copy the numbers or save them to your history.

faq.question: Can the minimum be larger than the maximum?
faq.answer: Yes, the tool automatically treats the smaller and larger values as the range bounds regardless of which field you type them into.

faq.question: What happens if I disallow duplicates but ask for too many numbers?
faq.answer: You'll see a warning and the Generate button is disabled, since your range doesn't contain enough unique numbers to fulfill the request without repeats.

faq.question: Is this suitable for a real lottery or raffle draw?
faq.answer: It's suitable for casual and low-stakes draws — for regulated or official drawings, check whether your jurisdiction requires a certified random number source.

faq.question: How many numbers can I generate at once?
faq.answer: Up to 1,000 numbers can be generated in a single batch.

faq.question: Does "allow duplicates" affect performance?
faq.answer: No, both modes generate instantly — duplicates just means each number is picked independently rather than removed from a shrinking pool.

faq.question: Can I generate negative numbers?
faq.answer: Yes, enter a negative minimum (or negative maximum) and the range works the same way with negative values included.

faq.question: Can I copy all the generated numbers at once?
faq.answer: Yes, the copy button copies every generated number as a single comma-separated list.

yes-no-decision-maker.seoTitle: Yes or No Decision Maker – Instant Random Answer
yes-no-decision-maker.metaDescription: Can't decide? Get an instant random yes or no answer — free, no sign-up, processed entirely in your browser.
yes-no-decision-maker.subheading: Get an instant random yes or no answer for any question you're stuck on.

howTo.name: Type your question (optional)
howTo.text: Enter what you're deciding on, just for your own reference.

howTo.name: Ask the decision maker
howTo.text: Click the button to get an instant random Yes or No.

howTo.name: See your answer
howTo.text: The result appears in the circle above the button.

howTo.name: Save if you'd like
howTo.text: Save the decision to your history along with your question.

faq.question: Is the answer truly 50/50?
faq.answer: Yes, each answer is chosen with an unweighted random draw, giving Yes and No an equal chance every time.

faq.question: Do I have to type a question?
faq.answer: No, the question field is optional — it's only there to help you remember what you were deciding on, and doesn't affect the random result.

faq.question: Can I get a different answer if I don't like it?
faq.answer: Yes, click the button again for a fresh independent random answer — there's no memory of previous results affecting the next one.

faq.question: Is my question stored or sent anywhere?
faq.answer: No, it stays in your browser and is only included in your local history if you explicitly click Save.

faq.question: Why is there a short delay before the answer appears?
faq.answer: A brief animation plays for about half a second before revealing the answer, purely for visual effect — the result itself is already determined instantly.

faq.question: Can I use this for more than two options?
faq.answer: No, this tool is specifically binary (yes/no) — use the Wheel Spinner or Random Name Picker for choosing between more than two options.

faq.question: Does it keep a running tally of yes vs no answers?
faq.answer: No, only the current answer is shown — for a running tally, check your saved history instead.

coin-flip.seoTitle: Coin Flip – Free Online Heads or Tails
coin-flip.metaDescription: Flip a virtual coin online — instant heads or tails with a running tally. Free, no sign-up, processed entirely in your browser.
coin-flip.subheading: Flip a virtual coin and keep a running tally of heads and tails.

howTo.name: Flip the coin
howTo.text: Click Flip the coin to get a random heads or tails result.

howTo.name: Watch the animation
howTo.text: The coin spins briefly before landing on its result.

howTo.name: Track your flips
howTo.text: Each flip is added to a running tally shown below the coin.

howTo.name: Save or reset
howTo.text: Save a result to your history, or reset the tally to start fresh.

faq.question: Is the coin flip fair (50/50)?
faq.answer: Yes, each flip is an independent, unweighted random choice between heads and tails.

faq.question: Does it remember my flip history between visits?
faq.answer: No, the running tally only persists for your current session — reloading the page resets it. Individual flips you Save are kept separately in your local history.

faq.question: How many times can I flip?
faq.answer: There's no limit — flip as many times as you like, and the tally keeps counting up.

faq.question: Can I flip multiple coins at once?
faq.answer: Yes. Set the Coins box to any number from 1 to 10 and every coin is flipped together; each result is added to the tally.

faq.question: What does the tally show exactly?
faq.answer: It shows the total count of heads, total count of tails, and the overall number of flips since your last reset.

faq.question: Can I clear the tally without reloading the page?
faq.answer: Yes, a "Reset tally" link appears once you've flipped at least once, which clears the count and flip history.

faq.question: Is this suitable for settling a real bet?
faq.answer: It's suitable for casual, friendly use — for anything with real stakes, a physical coin or a verifiable random source may be more appropriate.

dice-roller.seoTitle: Dice Roller – Roll Virtual Dice Online (d4 to d20)
dice-roller.metaDescription: Roll one or more virtual dice — d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, or d20 — with instant totals. Free, no sign-up, 100% private.
dice-roller.subheading: Roll virtual dice of any common size, with an instant total and roll history.

howTo.name: Pick your die size
howTo.text: Choose from d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, or d20.

howTo.name: Set how many dice
howTo.text: Enter the number of dice to roll at once.

howTo.name: Roll
howTo.text: Click Roll to get your random results and total.

howTo.name: Review or save
howTo.text: Check recent rolls below, or save a roll to your history.

faq.question: What die sizes are supported?
faq.answer: d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, and d20 — the standard set used in most tabletop games.

faq.question: How many dice can I roll at once?
faq.answer: Up to 20 dice in a single roll.

faq.question: Is each die roll independent?
faq.answer: Yes, every die in a roll is generated independently, so results aren't influenced by the other dice in the same roll.

faq.question: Does it keep a history of my rolls?
faq.answer: Yes, your most recent rolls are listed below the dice, showing each individual value and the total for that roll.

faq.question: Can I roll dice of different sizes in one roll?
faq.answer: No, all dice in a single roll use the same size — roll separately if you need to mix sizes, like 2d6 plus 1d20.

faq.question: Is this suitable for tabletop RPGs like D&D?
faq.answer: Yes, the standard polyhedral die sizes used in tabletop RPGs are all supported.

faq.question: Can I clear my roll history?
faq.answer: Yes, a Clear button next to the recent rolls list removes them from view.

list-shuffler.seoTitle: Random List Shuffler – Shuffle Any List Online
list-shuffler.metaDescription: Paste a list and instantly shuffle it into random order — free, no sign-up, processed entirely in your browser.
list-shuffler.subheading: Paste any list and shuffle it into a random order instantly.

howTo.name: Paste your list
howTo.text: Enter one item per line in the text box.

howTo.name: Shuffle
howTo.text: Click Shuffle to randomize the order.

howTo.name: Review the result
howTo.text: The shuffled list appears numbered below.

howTo.name: Copy or save
howTo.text: Copy the new order, or save it to your history.

faq.question: What shuffle algorithm is used?
faq.answer: A Fisher-Yates shuffle, which gives every possible ordering an equal, unbiased probability of occurring.

faq.question: Does shuffling remove duplicate items?
faq.answer: No, this tool only reorders your list — it doesn't remove duplicates. Use the Duplicate Line Remover first if you need both.

faq.question: How is this different from the Team Generator?
faq.answer: List Shuffler only reorders your items into a random sequence; Team Generator additionally splits the shuffled list into separate groups or teams.

faq.question: Can I shuffle the same list again for a different order?
faq.answer: Yes, click Shuffle again — each shuffle is independent, so you'll typically get a different order each time.

faq.question: Is there a limit to how many items I can shuffle?
faq.answer: No hard limit is enforced, though extremely large lists (thousands of lines) may take a moment longer since everything runs in your browser.

faq.question: Does it preserve blank lines or extra spacing?
faq.answer: No, blank lines are removed and each item is trimmed of leading/trailing whitespace before shuffling.

faq.question: Can I restore my original unshuffled list?
faq.answer: If you saved before shuffling, restoring that history entry brings back your original input — otherwise, re-type or re-paste it manually.

bracket-generator.seoTitle: Bracket Generator – Random Tournament Bracket Maker
bracket-generator.metaDescription: Paste a list of names or teams and generate a randomized single-elimination bracket — free, instant, no sign-up.
bracket-generator.subheading: Turn a list of entrants into a randomized single-elimination tournament bracket.

howTo.name: Enter your entrants
howTo.text: Type one name or team per line.

howTo.name: Generate the bracket
howTo.text: Click Generate bracket to create randomized round 1 matchups.

howTo.name: Review the matchups
howTo.text: Each match pairing is shown in order.

howTo.name: Copy or save
howTo.text: Copy the matchups or save them to your history.

faq.question: How are matchups decided?
faq.answer: Entrants are shuffled randomly first, then paired sequentially into matches — so seeding is entirely random, not based on any ranking.

faq.question: What happens if my entrant count isn't a power of two?
faq.answer: The bracket is padded with byes up to the next power of two (e.g. 6 entrants become an 8-slot bracket with 2 byes), and any entrant matched against a bye automatically advances.

faq.question: Does this generate later rounds too?
faq.answer: No, only round 1 matchups are generated — you'll need to record round 1 winners and generate later rounds separately as the tournament progresses.

faq.question: Can I seed entrants manually instead of randomly?
faq.answer: No, this tool only supports fully random seeding — for manual seeding, arrange matchups yourself after generating.

faq.question: Is there a graphical bracket diagram?
faq.answer: No, matchups are shown as a simple numbered list rather than a visual bracket tree.

faq.question: How many entrants can I include?
faq.answer: There's no hard limit, though very large entrant lists produce a correspondingly long match list to scroll through.

faq.question: Can I regenerate the bracket with a new random draw?
faq.answer: Yes, click Generate bracket again for a completely fresh random pairing.

raffle-picker.seoTitle: Raffle & Giveaway Picker – Draw Random Winners
raffle-picker.metaDescription: Draw one or more random raffle winners from a list of entries, with support for weighted entries — free, instant, no sign-up.
raffle-picker.subheading: Draw random winners from a list of raffle or giveaway entries.

howTo.name: Add your entries
howTo.text: Type one entry per line — repeat a name to give it more tickets.

howTo.name: Set the number of winners
howTo.text: Choose how many winners to draw.

howTo.name: Draw winners
howTo.text: Click Draw winners to run the random drawing.

howTo.name: Save the results
howTo.text: Copy the winners or save them to your history.

faq.question: How do I give someone extra chances of winning?
faq.answer: List their name multiple times — each repeated line acts as an extra ticket, proportionally increasing their odds.

faq.question: Can the same entry win more than once in one drawing?
faq.answer: No, drawing is without replacement, so once an entry (one ticket) is drawn as a winner, that specific ticket can't be drawn again in the same round.

faq.question: If I list someone 3 times and they win, are all 3 of their tickets removed?
faq.answer: No, only the one winning ticket is removed — their other tickets remain in the pool if you draw additional winners in the same round.

faq.question: What's the difference between this and the Random Name Picker?
faq.answer: This tool is built around a ticket/entry model that naturally supports weighting via repeated entries and a drawing animation, while Name Picker treats every name as an equal single entry.

faq.question: How many winners can I draw at once?
faq.answer: Up to the total number of entries you've listed — you can't draw more winners than there are tickets.

faq.question: Is my entry list private?
faq.answer: Yes, everything runs locally in your browser and is never uploaded anywhere.

faq.question: Is this suitable for a legally regulated raffle?
faq.answer: It's suitable for casual and informal giveaways — check your local regulations for anything requiring a certified or audited drawing process.

pomodoro-timer.seoTitle: Pomodoro Timer Online – Free Focus & Break Timer with Stats
pomodoro-timer.metaDescription: A free Pomodoro timer for studying and work: 25/5 focus and break cycles, long breaks, auto-start, sound and notifications, daily stats and fullscreen focus mode. Private, no sign-up.
pomodoro-timer.subheading: Stay focused with timed work sessions and short breaks — with a fullscreen focus mode, daily stats and a chime, all in your browser.

howTo.name: Pick your rhythm
howTo.text: Start with the classic 25 minutes of focus and 5 of rest, or choose Deep work 50/10 or Short 15/3. You can also type your own lengths.

howTo.name: Name your task
howTo.text: Write what you are working on so it shows under the clock. It helps you stay on one thing.

howTo.name: Press Start
howTo.text: The ring fills as time passes and the countdown also appears in your browser tab title, so you can see it from another tab.

howTo.name: Rest and repeat
howTo.text: When a session ends you hear a chime and the next phase starts. After four focus sessions you get a longer break. Check today's totals and the 7-day chart on the right.

faq.question: What is the Pomodoro Technique?
faq.answer: It is a time-management method: work in focused blocks of about 25 minutes, then take a 5-minute break. After four blocks, take a longer break of 15 to 30 minutes. The short deadlines make it easier to start and to resist distractions.

faq.question: Can I change the session lengths?
faq.answer: Yes. Set focus, short break, long break and how often the long break comes. Your choices are remembered on this device.

faq.question: Does it keep running if I switch tabs?
faq.answer: Yes. The timer is based on the real clock, not on counting ticks, so it stays accurate in a background tab. The remaining time is also shown in the tab title.

faq.question: Will it alert me when time is up?
faq.answer: It plays a short chime and can show a desktop notification if you allow notifications. You can turn either off.

faq.question: What does focus mode do?
faq.answer: It makes the timer fill your whole screen with a large clock and nothing else, which is useful on a second monitor or a tablet next to your books.

faq.question: Is my data uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your settings, task name and statistics are stored only in your browser and never sent anywhere. Clearing your browser data removes them.

faq.question: Which break length is best?
faq.answer: There is no single answer. The classic 25/5 works for most people. If you like long, deep sessions try 50/10. Short 15-minute sessions can help when you find it hard to begin.

focus-sounds.seoTitle: Focus Sounds & Noise Mixer – Free White, Brown Noise, Rain for Studying
focus-sounds.metaDescription: Mix 24 calming sounds — rain, thunder, ocean, birds, café, train, fire, white, pink and brown noise, and binaural beats — to concentrate, study or sleep. Tone controls, sleep timer, saved mixes. Generated in your browser, no downloads.
focus-sounds.subheading: Blend rain, thunder, café ambience, brown noise, binaural beats and more into your own background mix to block distractions while you study, work or sleep.

howTo.name: Pick a sound
howTo.text: Tap a card such as Rain, Brown noise or Café to switch it on, or filter by Nature, Noise, Rooms or Tones and beats. Use a Quick mix like Deep focus, or press Surprise me.

howTo.name: Mix the levels
howTo.text: Move each slider to set how loud that sound is, and the master volume for everything. Open Tone and fade to adjust bass, treble and brightness and the fade-in time.

howTo.name: Set a sleep timer
howTo.text: Choose a time and the sound fades out and stops by itself — handy when you listen while falling asleep.

howTo.name: Keep working
howTo.text: Save your favourite mixes with a name. They are remembered on this device, so next time you only need to press Play mix.

faq.question: Which sound is best for concentration?
faq.answer: It differs between people. Brown noise is deep and warm and many find it good for focus. Pink noise is more balanced. Rain and ocean waves feel natural and calming. White noise is brightest and masks speech well.

faq.question: Do the sounds need an internet connection?
faq.answer: No. Every sound is created live in your browser with the Web Audio API. There is nothing to download or stream, so it works offline after the page has loaded.

faq.question: What are binaural beats?
faq.answer: Two slightly different tones are played, one in each ear. The difference (for example 10 Hz for alpha) is the beat. Some people find them relaxing or helpful for focus. You need headphones for it to work, and the science is mixed, so treat it as an option rather than a promise.

faq.question: Why can't I hear anything?
faq.answer: Browsers only start audio after you click. Press Play mix, check your device volume and the master slider, and make sure at least one sound has a volume above zero.

faq.question: Is it safe to play all night?
faq.answer: Keep the volume low and use the sleep timer. Loud noise for long periods can be tiring for your ears.

faq.question: Is my mix saved?
faq.answer: Yes, on this device only. It is stored in your browser and never uploaded.

faq.question: Can I use it together with a timer?
faq.answer: Yes. Open the Pomodoro Timer in another tab and keep the sounds playing while you work.

flashcards.seoTitle: Flashcard Maker with Spaced Repetition – Free Online Study Cards
flashcards.metaDescription: Make flashcard decks, import cards from text, and study with a spaced-repetition (Leitner) schedule. Flip cards, track progress, export your deck. Free, private, works offline.
flashcards.subheading: Build decks, flip through cards, and let the schedule bring back the ones you miss — stored only on your device.

howTo.name: Create a deck
howTo.text: Type a deck name and press Create deck, or choose Import cards and paste a list with one question and answer per line.

howTo.name: Add your cards
howTo.text: Fill in the front and back and press Enter to add each card quickly. You can edit or delete any card later.

howTo.name: Study
howTo.text: Press Study to see the cards that are due. Click the card or press Space to flip it, then choose Got it or Missed it (keys 2 and 1).

howTo.name: Come back tomorrow
howTo.text: Cards you know move to a later box and return after more days. Missed cards come back soon. Export the deck any time to back it up.

faq.question: What is spaced repetition?
faq.answer: It is a way of reviewing information just before you would forget it. Cards you know well are shown less often and cards you find hard are shown more often, which saves time and builds long-term memory.

faq.question: How does the schedule work?
faq.answer: It uses the Leitner system with five boxes. A correct answer moves a card up a box and it returns after 1, 2, 4, 8 and then 16 days. A wrong answer sends it back to the first box so you see it again today.

faq.question: How do I import cards?
faq.answer: Paste one card per line with the question and answer separated by a tab, a comma, a semicolon or a space-dash-space. This works with lists copied from spreadsheets and most notes apps.

faq.question: Can I back up or move my decks?
faq.answer: Yes. Open a deck, press Export, and you get a tab-separated file that you can import again here or open in a spreadsheet.

faq.question: Where are my cards stored?
faq.answer: Only in your browser's local storage on this device. Nothing is uploaded, so clearing browser data deletes your decks — export first if they matter.

faq.question: Can I study everything, not only due cards?
faq.answer: Yes. The All button shuffles every card in the deck, which is useful the night before an exam.

faq.question: Does it support images or other languages?
faq.answer: Cards are text, and any language or symbol your device can display works, including right-to-left scripts and maths symbols.

eisenhower-matrix.seoTitle: Eisenhower Matrix – Free Priority Matrix & To-Do Planner Online
eisenhower-matrix.metaDescription: Sort tasks into the Eisenhower matrix: do first, schedule, delegate or eliminate. Drag and drop, check off, copy as text. Free, private, saved in your browser.
eisenhower-matrix.subheading: Decide what to do now, what to plan, what to hand off and what to drop — drag your tasks into four boxes.

howTo.name: Add your tasks
howTo.text: Type a task into the box where it belongs and press Enter. You can start with a brain dump and sort later.

howTo.name: Sort by urgency and importance
howTo.text: Drag tasks between the four boxes, or use the small menu on a task. Urgent and important goes in Do first.

howTo.name: Work from the top
howTo.text: Finish Do first, book time for Schedule, hand off Delegate and be honest about Eliminate.

howTo.name: Check off and share
howTo.text: Tick tasks as you complete them, clear finished ones, or copy the whole matrix as text to paste into notes or a message.

faq.question: What is the Eisenhower matrix?
faq.answer: It is a way to prioritise by sorting tasks on two questions: is it urgent, and is it important? The answer tells you whether to do it now, schedule it, delegate it or drop it.

faq.question: What goes in each box?
faq.answer: Do first: urgent and important, like a deadline tomorrow. Schedule: important but not urgent, like revision or exercise. Delegate: urgent but not important, like some requests and interruptions. Eliminate: neither, like time-wasting habits.

faq.question: How many tasks should be in Do first?
faq.answer: As few as possible. If this box is always full, planning more in Schedule usually helps, because well-planned work becomes less urgent.

faq.question: Can I use it on a phone?
faq.answer: Yes. Dragging works on many devices, and every task also has a small menu to move it to another box.

faq.question: Is my list saved?
faq.answer: Yes, in your browser on this device only. It is not uploaded, and clearing browser data removes it.

faq.question: Can I export the matrix?
faq.answer: Press Copy as text to get all four boxes as a checklist you can paste anywhere.

faq.question: Why do I need to separate urgent from important?
faq.answer: Urgent things shout for attention, but important things move your goals forward. Seeing them in separate boxes helps you stop reacting all day and start planning.

exam-countdown.seoTitle: Exam & Deadline Countdown – Free Days Until Timer for Students
exam-countdown.metaDescription: Count down to exams, deadlines and trips with live days, hours, minutes and seconds. Add many events, colour-coded by urgency. Free and private, saved in your browser.
exam-countdown.subheading: See exactly how much time is left until your next exam, deadline or trip, with live days, hours, minutes and seconds.

howTo.name: Name the event
howTo.text: Type what you are counting down to, for example Chemistry final.

howTo.name: Choose the date and time
howTo.text: Pick the exact moment, or tap a quick choice such as Tomorrow, In a week or In 100 days.

howTo.name: Watch the clock
howTo.text: The nearest event is shown big, with a colour that goes from green to amber to red as it gets closer.

howTo.name: Plan backwards
howTo.text: Use the number of days left to split your revision into daily goals. Past events are tucked away under Past.

faq.question: Can I count down to more than one date?
faq.answer: Yes. Add as many exams and deadlines as you like. They are sorted with the nearest first.

faq.question: What do the colours mean?
faq.answer: Green means more than two weeks away, amber means within two weeks and red means within three days. Past events are grey.

faq.question: Is the time zone handled correctly?
faq.answer: The date and time you choose are in your device's local time zone, and the countdown uses the same clock.

faq.question: Does it keep counting when the page is closed?
faq.answer: The page must be open to show the live seconds, but your events are saved, so the correct time left appears as soon as you open it again.

faq.question: Are my events uploaded?
faq.answer: No. They are stored only in your browser on this device.

faq.question: How should I use the days left?
faq.answer: Divide the topics you still have to cover by the days left. A countdown makes the deadline real and helps you start earlier.

faq.question: Can I use it for non-study events?
faq.answer: Yes. It works for any date: a flight, a birthday, a product launch or a holiday.

habit-tracker.seoTitle: Habit Tracker – Free Daily Streak Tracker for Study & Routines
habit-tracker.metaDescription: Track daily habits like studying, reading or exercise. Check off days, see current and best streaks, 30-day completion and a 5-week heat map. Free and private.
habit-tracker.subheading: Build a routine one day at a time — check off your habits, keep your streak alive and see your progress.

howTo.name: Add a habit
howTo.text: Type a small, specific habit such as Review notes for 20 minutes, or tap one of the suggestions.

howTo.name: Check it off
howTo.text: Each day, tap the day in the week row. Tap again to undo. You can also fill in a missed day.

howTo.name: Protect your streak
howTo.text: The flame shows how many days in a row you have done it. If you have not checked today yet, yesterday's streak still counts.

howTo.name: Review your progress
howTo.text: See your best streak, the share of the last 30 days you completed, and a 5-week heat map for each habit.

faq.question: How are streaks counted?
faq.answer: A streak is the number of consecutive days that are checked, ending today. If today is not checked yet, the streak ending yesterday is still shown so you do not lose it before the day is over.

faq.question: What makes a good habit?
faq.answer: Small and specific. Twenty minutes of revision is easier to repeat than study more. Link it to something you already do, like after breakfast.

faq.question: Can I edit past days?
faq.answer: Yes. Tap any day in the last seven days to turn it on or off.

faq.question: How many habits should I track?
faq.answer: Two to five is plenty. Too many make it hard to keep up, and a missed day can feel like failure.

faq.question: Is my data private?
faq.answer: Yes. Habits are stored only in your browser on this device. Nothing is uploaded or shared.

faq.question: What if I break my streak?
faq.answer: Start again today. The best streak is kept, and the 30-day completion rate shows that a missed day does not erase your progress.

faq.question: Does it work with the Pomodoro timer?
faq.answer: They fit well together: add a habit like Two focus sessions and check it off after your timer finishes.

stretch-break.seoTitle: Desk Stretch Break – Free Guided Stretching Routines for Work & Study
stretch-break.metaDescription: Guided stretch breaks with a timer for each move: desk reset, neck and shoulders, wrists and hands, and eye rest 20-20-20. Free, private, no sign-up.
stretch-break.subheading: Loosen up after long sessions with timed, step-by-step stretches for your neck, shoulders, wrists and eyes.

howTo.name: Choose a routine
howTo.text: Pick Desk reset for a full loosen-up, Neck & shoulders, Wrists & hands, or Eye rest 20-20-20.

howTo.name: Follow each step
howTo.text: The screen shows the move, a short instruction and a countdown ring. A soft chime tells you when to change.

howTo.name: Pause or skip
howTo.text: Use Pause if you need a moment, or the arrows to go back or ahead.

howTo.name: Make it a habit
howTo.text: Each finished routine adds to today's break count. Try one after every two Pomodoro sessions.

faq.question: How often should I stretch while studying or working?
faq.answer: A short break every 30 to 60 minutes is a good rule. Even one or two minutes of moving helps your neck, back and eyes, and it also helps you concentrate when you return.

faq.question: Do I need any equipment or space?
faq.answer: No. Every move can be done sitting at a desk or standing next to it. Wear whatever you are comfortable in.

faq.question: What is the 20-20-20 rule?
faq.answer: Every 20 minutes, look at something about 20 feet (6 metres) away for at least 20 seconds. It rests the muscles inside your eyes and reduces strain from screens.

faq.question: Is stretching safe for everyone?
faq.answer: Stretches should feel like gentle tension, never pain. Stop if something hurts. If you have an injury or a medical condition, ask a doctor or physiotherapist first. This tool is general wellness information, not medical advice.

faq.question: Can I use it with the Pomodoro timer?
faq.answer: Yes. Many people use the short break after a focus session to do a one-minute routine. Open the Pomodoro Timer in another tab and switch between them.

faq.question: Is anything stored or uploaded?
faq.answer: Only the number of breaks you finish each day is saved, in your browser on this device. Nothing is uploaded.

faq.question: Does it work in fullscreen?
faq.answer: Yes. Press Fullscreen to get large text and a big timer, which is handy on a tablet or a second screen.

breathing-exercise.seoTitle: Breathing Exercise Timer – Free Box Breathing & 4-7-8 Relaxation Tool
breathing-exercise.metaDescription: A guided breathing timer with an animated circle: box breathing, 4-7-8, coherent 5-5 and long exhale. Calm down between study sessions. Free and private.
breathing-exercise.subheading: Follow the circle to breathe in, hold and out in a steady rhythm — to calm down, reset your focus or wind down for sleep.

howTo.name: Pick a pattern
howTo.text: Box breathing is steady and focused, 4-7-8 is deeply calming, Coherent 5-5 is gentle and even, and Long exhale helps release tension.

howTo.name: Choose how long
howTo.text: Select 1, 3, 5 or 10 minutes.

howTo.name: Press Start
howTo.text: Breathe in as the circle grows, hold when it says Hold, and breathe out as it shrinks. The number shows seconds left in each step.

howTo.name: Finish with a chime
howTo.text: When time is up a soft chime plays. Reset or choose another pattern any time.

faq.question: What is box breathing?
faq.answer: It is a pattern of equal parts: breathe in for four seconds, hold four, breathe out four and rest four. People use it to feel calm and steady, for example before a test or a presentation.

faq.question: What is 4-7-8 breathing?
faq.answer: Breathe in through the nose for four seconds, hold for seven, and breathe out slowly for eight. The long exhale is very relaxing, so many people use it to unwind or fall asleep.

faq.question: Does breathing exercise really help?
faq.answer: Slow breathing with a longer out-breath can lower your heart rate and help you feel calmer for a while. It is a simple relaxation technique, not a treatment. If you feel dizzy, breathe normally. Speak to a doctor about anxiety or breathing problems.

faq.question: How long should I do it?
faq.answer: Three to five minutes is plenty for a break. One minute still helps when you are short of time.

faq.question: How should I breathe?
faq.answer: Sit comfortably, relax your shoulders, and breathe through your nose if that is easy. Let your belly move gently. Never force or strain.

faq.question: Can I use it with focus sounds?
faq.answer: Yes. Start the Focus Sounds mixer with rain or ocean waves in another tab and breathe along with the circle.

faq.question: Is my data stored?
faq.answer: No. Nothing is saved or uploaded. The tool just runs a timer in your browser.

memory-match.seoTitle: Memory Match Game – Free Online Card Matching Game for Brain Breaks
memory-match.metaDescription: Play a free memory card matching game with three difficulty levels. Flip cards, find pairs, track moves and time, and beat your best score. Great for a short break.
memory-match.subheading: Flip the cards and find all the matching pairs in as few moves as you can — a quick brain break between study sessions.

howTo.name: Pick a level
howTo.text: Easy has 6 pairs, Medium 8 and Hard 12.

howTo.name: Flip two cards
howTo.text: Click a card to turn it over, then a second one. If they match they stay face up; if not they flip back.

howTo.name: Remember the positions
howTo.text: Use your memory to find pairs with fewer moves. The timer starts on your first flip.

howTo.name: Beat your best
howTo.text: Finish all pairs to earn up to three stars. Your best score for each level is saved on this device.

faq.question: How do I win?
faq.answer: Find all the matching pairs. Fewer moves and a shorter time give you a better score and more stars.

faq.question: Does it improve memory?
faq.answer: Games like this exercise short-term visual memory and attention, and they are a fun way to rest your mind. They are not a medical treatment, and results in the game do not prove changes in everyday memory.

faq.question: What do the stars mean?
faq.answer: Three stars means you finished in very few moves, close to the number of pairs. Two stars is a good game, and one star means you needed many tries — just play again.

faq.question: Can I play on a phone?
faq.answer: Yes. The cards are large and work with touch. In fullscreen they get even bigger.

faq.question: Is my score saved?
faq.answer: Your best moves and time for each level are stored in your browser on this device only.

faq.question: Why a game on a study site?
faq.answer: Short, low-pressure games help your brain rest between focus sessions. Keep it to a few minutes, then go back to work.

faq.question: Is it free?
faq.answer: Yes. It is free, has no ads inside the game and needs no account.

reaction-time-test.seoTitle: Reaction Time Test – Free Online Reflex Speed Test in Milliseconds
reaction-time-test.metaDescription: Test your reaction time in milliseconds. Click when the screen turns green, play five rounds, see your average and save your best. Free, private, no sign-up.
reaction-time-test.subheading: Click as soon as the screen turns green. Five rounds give you your average reaction time in milliseconds.

howTo.name: Start the test
howTo.text: Click the red area to begin a round.

howTo.name: Wait for green
howTo.text: The screen turns red, then green after a random pause. Don't click while it is red.

howTo.name: Click fast
howTo.text: As soon as it turns green, click or tap. Your time in milliseconds appears.

howTo.name: Finish five rounds
howTo.text: After five rounds you see your average. Your best average is saved on this device.

faq.question: What is a good reaction time?
faq.answer: For a visual test like this, most people average between 200 and 300 milliseconds. Under 200 ms is very fast. Your result also depends on your screen, mouse and device.

faq.question: Why does it say Too soon?
faq.answer: You clicked before the screen turned green. The wait is random on purpose so you can't guess it. Just click to try again.

faq.question: Does tiredness change my reaction time?
faq.answer: Yes. Lack of sleep, a long work session or distraction usually slows reactions. That is why it makes a simple check of how rested you feel.

faq.question: Is it accurate?
faq.answer: It measures from the moment the screen changes to your click, but your display refresh rate, input device and browser add a few milliseconds. It is great for comparing yourself over time, not for lab results.

faq.question: Is my best score saved?
faq.answer: Yes, your best average is saved in your browser on this device. Use Reset to clear it.

faq.question: Can I use it on a touch screen?
faq.answer: Yes, tap anywhere in the coloured area. Touch screens often add a little extra delay.

faq.question: Is anything uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Everything runs in your browser.

game-2048.seoTitle: 2048 Game – Free Online 2048 Puzzle with Undo and Touch Controls
game-2048.metaDescription: Play 2048 free in your browser. Slide and merge tiles to reach 2048 with keyboard, WASD or swipe, with undo and a saved best score. A relaxing break from studying.
game-2048.subheading: Slide the tiles, join equal numbers and try to reach 2048 — a classic puzzle for a short, calming break.

howTo.name: Move the tiles
howTo.text: Use the arrow keys or W, A, S, D on a keyboard, or swipe on a touch screen. All tiles slide in that direction.

howTo.name: Merge equal numbers
howTo.text: When two tiles with the same number touch, they join into one with their sum.

howTo.name: Plan ahead
howTo.text: Keep your biggest tile in a corner and keep the board tidy. A new 2 or 4 appears after every move.

howTo.name: Reach 2048
howTo.text: Build the 2048 tile to win, then keep going for a higher score. Undo takes back your last move.

faq.question: What is the goal of 2048?
faq.answer: Create a tile with the number 2048 by merging equal tiles. You can keep playing afterwards to get a higher score.

faq.question: Which strategy works best?
faq.answer: Keep your largest tile in one corner, build a row of descending numbers beside it, and avoid moving in the direction that pulls the big tile out of the corner.

faq.question: When does the game end?
faq.answer: When the board is full and no two neighbouring tiles are equal, so no move is possible.

faq.question: Can I undo a move?
faq.answer: Yes. Press Undo to take back your last move. It only remembers one step.

faq.question: Does it work on a phone?
faq.answer: Yes. Swipe on the board. Fullscreen makes the board bigger.

faq.question: Is my best score saved?
faq.answer: Yes, on this device only, in your browser's local storage. Nothing is uploaded.

faq.question: Is it a good study break?
faq.answer: A few minutes of a calm puzzle can rest your mind. Because it is easy to keep playing, set a short timer so your break stays a break.

todo-list.seoTitle: To-Do List Online – Free Task List with Priorities & Due Dates
todo-list.metaDescription: A free online to-do list with priorities, due dates, filters and a progress bar. Tasks are saved automatically in your browser — no account, no sign-up, private.
todo-list.subheading: Write down your tasks, set a priority and a due date, and tick them off. Everything saves automatically on your device.

howTo.name: Add a task
howTo.text: Type what you need to do, choose High, Medium or Low priority, optionally pick a due date, and press Enter.

howTo.name: Work from the top
howTo.text: Tasks are sorted by priority and due date, with finished tasks at the bottom. Overdue tasks turn red.

howTo.name: Tick and edit
howTo.text: Press the circle to mark a task as done. Click a task's text to rename it.

howTo.name: Clean up
howTo.text: Use Completed to review finished tasks and Clear completed to remove them. Your progress bar shows how much is done.

faq.question: Is my to-do list saved?
faq.answer: Yes. It is saved automatically in your browser's local storage on this device, so it is still there when you come back. It is never uploaded, and clearing your browser data removes it.

faq.question: Can I use it on my phone and computer?
faq.answer: The list lives in one browser on one device. To use it somewhere else, open the page there — it will start empty, because nothing is sent online.

faq.question: How are tasks ordered?
faq.answer: Unfinished tasks come first, then by priority (High, Medium, Low), then by earliest due date.

faq.question: What does Overdue mean?
faq.answer: A task with a due date earlier than today that is not finished. It is shown in red so you notice it.

faq.question: Can I edit a task?
faq.answer: Yes. Click the task text, change it and press Enter.

faq.question: Is there a limit to the number of tasks?
faq.answer: No fixed limit. Browsers allow several megabytes of local storage, which is room for thousands of tasks.

faq.question: Does it work with the Pomodoro timer?
faq.answer: Yes. Pick a task, then run a Pomodoro session on it in the Pomodoro Timer tool.

study-time-tracker.seoTitle: Study Time Tracker – Free Study Log with Timer and Weekly Chart
study-time-tracker.metaDescription: Track how long you study each subject with a one-click timer or manual entries. See today, this week and all-time totals, a 7-day chart, and export to CSV. Private and saved locally.
study-time-tracker.subheading: Start a timer for a subject, see where your hours go, and build a clear picture of your week.

howTo.name: Pick a subject
howTo.text: Choose one of the subjects or add your own, such as Maths or Reading.

howTo.name: Start studying
howTo.text: Press Start studying. The timer keeps running even if you reload the page. Press Stop & save when you finish.

howTo.name: Add missed time
howTo.text: If you forgot to start the timer, add minutes manually to a subject.

howTo.name: Review and export
howTo.text: See today, this week and all-time totals per subject, the 7-day chart and recent sessions. Download everything as a CSV file.

faq.question: Where is my study data stored?
faq.answer: In your browser's local storage on this device only. Nothing is uploaded. Clearing your browser data deletes it, so export a CSV if you want a backup.

faq.question: Does the timer keep going if I close the tab?
faq.answer: Yes. The start time is saved, so when you open the page again the timer shows the correct elapsed time. Press Stop & save to record the session.

faq.question: Can I track several subjects?
faq.answer: Yes. Add as many subjects as you like. Each has its own colour and totals.

faq.question: How is the week calculated?
faq.answer: The last seven days including today, based on the date each session started.

faq.question: Can I delete a wrong entry?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the bin icon next to a session in Recent sessions.

faq.question: What is in the CSV?
faq.answer: The start date and time, subject, minutes and note for every session, ready for a spreadsheet.

faq.question: How much should I study?
faq.answer: It depends on your goals. Regular, focused sessions with breaks work better than very long ones. Use the Pomodoro Timer to structure them.

daily-journal.seoTitle: Daily Journal & Mood Tracker – Free Private Online Diary
daily-journal.metaDescription: A private daily journal with mood tracking, gratitude and wins, a week view, search and streaks. Saved only in your browser — no account, nothing uploaded. Export anytime.
daily-journal.subheading: Check in with a few lines a day: your mood, what you are grateful for and what went well. Private and saved on your device.

howTo.name: Pick the day
howTo.text: Today is open by default. Tap another day in the week strip or choose any past date.

howTo.name: Choose your mood
howTo.text: Tap one of five faces from Rough to Great. Tap again to clear it.

howTo.name: Write a little
howTo.text: Add what you are grateful for, your wins and any notes. It saves as you type.

howTo.name: Look back
howTo.text: Search your entries, see your streak and average mood, and export everything as a text file.

faq.question: Is my journal private?
faq.answer: Yes. Entries are stored only in your browser's local storage on this device. They are not uploaded, and there is no account. Anyone who can open this browser on your device could read them, so use a device lock.

faq.question: Can I lose my entries?
faq.answer: Clearing your browser data or using a different browser or device will remove or hide them. Use Export now and then to keep a backup.

faq.question: Why keep a gratitude journal?
faq.answer: Writing down a few good things each day is a simple habit that many people find lifts their mood. It is a wellbeing practice, not medical advice.

faq.question: What is the streak?
faq.answer: The number of days in a row you wrote something, ending today or yesterday.

faq.question: Can I write for past days?
faq.answer: Yes. Pick a date from the calendar field or tap an entry in the list.

faq.question: Does it track my mood over time?
faq.answer: It shows your average mood across entries and the face for each day in the week strip.

faq.question: Is it suitable for mental health support?
faq.answer: It is a reflection tool only. If you feel very low or unsafe, please talk to someone you trust or a mental health professional.

math-speed-trainer.seoTitle: Mental Math Speed Trainer – Free 60-Second Arithmetic Practice Game
math-speed-trainer.metaDescription: Practise addition, subtraction, multiplication and division against the clock. Choose operations and difficulty, see score and accuracy, and beat your best. Free, saved locally.
math-speed-trainer.subheading: Answer as many sums as you can in 60 seconds. Pick the operations and the level, and try to beat your best.

howTo.name: Choose operations
howTo.text: Tick any of + − × ÷. At least one must stay on.

howTo.name: Pick a level
howTo.text: Easy uses small numbers, Medium goes up to 20 and tables to 10, and Hard goes to 100 and tables to 12.

howTo.name: Answer fast
howTo.text: Type the answer and press Enter. A new question appears straight away.

howTo.name: Beat your best
howTo.text: When 60 seconds are up you see your score and accuracy. Your best for each setting is saved on this device.

faq.question: Are the questions always whole numbers?
faq.answer: Yes. Subtraction never goes below zero and division always has an exact whole-number answer.

faq.question: Is my best score saved?
faq.answer: Yes, separately for each combination of operations and level, in your browser on this device.

faq.question: What is a good score?
faq.answer: It depends on the level. Aim to improve a little each time. Accuracy matters as much as speed.

faq.question: How can it help my studying?
faq.answer: Short daily drills build fluency with basic facts, which frees up your attention for harder problems.

faq.question: Can I practise only times tables?
faq.answer: Yes. Turn on only × and choose a level. Hard covers tables up to 12.

faq.question: Does it work on a phone?
faq.answer: Yes. A number keypad appears on most phones when you tap the answer box.

faq.question: Is anything sent online?
faq.answer: No. The questions are made in your browser and your scores stay on your device.

typing-speed-test.seoTitle: Typing Speed Test – Free WPM and Accuracy Test with History
typing-speed-test.metaDescription: Test your typing speed in words per minute with 30, 60 or 120 second tests. See live WPM and accuracy and track your last results. Free, private, saved in your browser.
typing-speed-test.subheading: Type the passage as fast and accurately as you can and get your words per minute and accuracy.

howTo.name: Pick a length
howTo.text: Choose 30, 60 or 120 seconds.

howTo.name: Start typing
howTo.text: Click the text and type. The timer starts with your first key, and each letter turns green or red.

howTo.name: Read your result
howTo.text: When time is up, or you reach the end of the passage, you see your words per minute and accuracy.

howTo.name: Track progress
howTo.text: Your last results are listed on the right so you can see yourself improve.

faq.question: How is WPM calculated?
faq.answer: Every five correct characters count as one word, divided by the minutes taken. Only correctly typed characters count.

faq.question: What is a good typing speed?
faq.answer: Many people type 35 to 45 WPM. Above 60 is quick and above 80 is very fast. Accuracy matters more than raw speed.

faq.question: Why does accuracy matter?
faq.answer: Mistakes cost time to fix. Typing a little slower with fewer errors usually gets you further than rushing.

faq.question: Can I fix a mistake?
faq.answer: You can delete with Backspace. Characters you typed wrong show in red until you correct them.

faq.question: Are my results saved?
faq.answer: The last 20 results are kept in your browser on this device only. Use Clear to remove them.

faq.question: Does it work with other keyboard layouts?
faq.answer: Yes, but the passages are in English, so you need to be able to type English letters and punctuation.

faq.question: Is anything uploaded?
faq.answer: No. The test runs fully in your browser.

snake-game.seoTitle: Snake Game – Free Classic Snake Online with Touch Controls
snake-game.metaDescription: Play the classic Snake game free in your browser. Arrow keys, WASD or swipe, three speeds, saved best score and fullscreen. A relaxing break from studying.
snake-game.subheading: Guide the snake to eat the food without hitting the walls or yourself. A classic, quick break.

howTo.name: Start
howTo.text: Press Start or any arrow key. The snake begins moving to the right.

howTo.name: Steer
howTo.text: Use the arrow keys or W, A, S, D on a keyboard, or swipe on a touch screen. You can't turn straight back on yourself.

howTo.name: Eat and grow
howTo.text: Eat the red food to score a point and grow longer.

howTo.name: Avoid crashes
howTo.text: The game ends if you touch a wall or your own body. Beat your saved best score.

faq.question: What are the controls?
faq.answer: Arrow keys or W, A, S, D to steer, Space to pause, and swipe on a phone or tablet.

faq.question: Can I change the speed?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose Chill, Normal or Fast. Faster speeds are harder.

faq.question: Is my best score saved?
faq.answer: Yes, in your browser on this device only.

faq.question: Does the snake wrap around the edges?
faq.answer: No. Touching the edge ends the game, which makes it a little harder.

faq.question: Does it work on a phone?
faq.answer: Yes. Swipe on the board to turn. Fullscreen gives you a bigger board.

faq.question: Is it a good study break?
faq.answer: A few minutes can clear your head. Set a short timer so your break doesn't turn into an hour.

faq.question: Does it cost anything?
faq.answer: No. It is free, has no ads in the game and needs no account.

schulte-table.seoTitle: Schulte Table – Free Attention & Peripheral Vision Training Game
schulte-table.metaDescription: Train your attention and speed with a Schulte table: find the numbers 1 to 25 in order as fast as you can. Four grid sizes, a timer and saved best times. Free and private.
schulte-table.subheading: Find the numbers in order as fast as you can while keeping your eyes in the middle — a classic way to train focus and peripheral vision.

howTo.name: Choose a grid
howTo.text: Pick 3×3, 4×4, 5×5 or 6×6. The 5×5 table is the classic.

howTo.name: Start with 1
howTo.text: Tap the number 1 to start the timer, then find 2, 3, 4 and so on in order.

howTo.name: Keep your eyes in the centre
howTo.text: Try to look at the middle of the table and spot the next number with your side vision.

howTo.name: Beat your time
howTo.text: When you reach the last number your time is saved if it is your best for that size.

faq.question: What is a Schulte table?
faq.answer: A grid of numbers placed in random order. You find them one by one in sequence. It was designed to train attention, visual search and peripheral vision.

faq.question: Does it help with speed reading?
faq.answer: Many people use it as a warm-up for speed reading because it practises taking in information without moving your eyes much. Results vary and it is not a medical treatment.

faq.question: What is a good time?
faq.answer: For the 5×5 table, under 30 seconds is good and under 20 is very fast. Compare yourself with your own earlier times.

faq.question: Why does a wrong tap flash red?
faq.answer: You tapped a number that is not the next one. Nothing is lost; just find the right number.

faq.question: Are my best times saved?
faq.answer: Yes, for each grid size, in your browser on this device only.

faq.question: How often should I practise?
faq.answer: A few short rounds a day are enough. Stop when you feel tired.

faq.question: Does it work on a phone?
faq.answer: Yes. The numbers are large and respond to touch.

stroop-test.seoTitle: Stroop Test – Free Online Colour-Word Focus and Self-Control Game
stroop-test.metaDescription: Take the Stroop test: a word is shown in a colour and you tap the colour of the ink, not what the word says. 30-second rounds, score and accuracy, saved best. Free and private.
stroop-test.subheading: Name the colour of the ink, not the word — a quick test of focus, attention and self-control.

howTo.name: Read the rules
howTo.text: A colour word appears, printed in a colour that is often different from the word.

howTo.name: Tap the ink colour
howTo.text: Tap the button for the colour you see, not the word you read. You can also press 1, 2, 3 or 4.

howTo.name: Be quick and careful
howTo.text: You have 30 seconds. Wrong answers do not cost points, but they lower your accuracy.

howTo.name: Check your score
howTo.text: See how many you got right and your accuracy. Your best score is saved.

faq.question: What is the Stroop effect?
faq.answer: It is the delay and mistakes that happen when the meaning of a word (such as RED) conflicts with the colour it is printed in (such as blue). Your brain has to ignore the automatic reading.

faq.question: What does the test measure?
faq.answer: Selective attention and the ability to suppress an automatic response. It is a classic test in psychology.

faq.question: Can practice improve my score?
faq.answer: Yes, people usually get faster and more accurate with practice. That does not prove a lasting change in everyday thinking.

faq.question: Why are most words in the wrong colour?
faq.answer: On purpose. Most trials show a different word and colour to create the conflict; some match so you cannot predict.

faq.question: Is my best score saved?
faq.answer: Yes, in your browser on this device only.

faq.question: Is it a medical test?
faq.answer: No. It is a fun exercise, not a diagnosis.

faq.question: Is the test colour-blind friendly?
faq.answer: The buttons are labelled with the colour names. If you have trouble telling colours apart, rely on the labels.

n-back-game.seoTitle: N-Back Game – Free Working Memory Training (1-back, 2-back, 3-back)
n-back-game.metaDescription: Train your working memory with the n-back task: a square lights up on a 3×3 grid and you press Match when it is in the same place as n steps earlier. Three levels, scores saved. Free.
n-back-game.subheading: Watch the squares light up and press Match when one is in the same place as n steps ago — a well-known working memory exercise.

howTo.name: Choose a level
howTo.text: 1-back is the easiest. 2-back and 3-back are harder.

howTo.name: Watch the grid
howTo.text: One square at a time lights up on a 3×3 grid every couple of seconds.

howTo.name: Press Match
howTo.text: Press Match or the Space bar when the square is in the same position as n steps earlier. Do nothing otherwise.

howTo.name: Read your results
howTo.text: After 24 rounds you see hits, misses, false alarms and your accuracy.

faq.question: What is the n-back task?
faq.answer: A test where you compare the current item with the one shown n steps earlier. It keeps your working memory constantly busy.

faq.question: What does 2-back mean?
faq.answer: You compare the current square with the one two steps before. Remember the last two positions and update them every time.

faq.question: Does n-back make me smarter?
faq.answer: Research is mixed. It reliably improves your n-back performance; transfer to everyday tasks is debated. Treat it as a mental workout, not a guarantee.

faq.question: What is a false alarm?
faq.answer: Pressing Match when there was no match.

faq.question: Is my best score saved?
faq.answer: Yes, per level, in your browser on this device only.

faq.question: Why is it hard?
faq.answer: You must hold and update several positions at once while new ones arrive. It is meant to be demanding.

faq.question: Can I use the keyboard?
faq.answer: Yes. Press the Space bar or Enter for Match.

simon-game.seoTitle: Simon Game – Free Online Memory Pattern Game with Sound
simon-game.metaDescription: Play the Simon memory game online: watch the colour and sound pattern, then repeat it. The sequence gets longer every round. Saved best score, works on phone. Free.
simon-game.subheading: Watch the pattern of lights and sounds, then repeat it — each round adds one more step.

howTo.name: Press Start
howTo.text: The game lights up one pad and plays its sound.

howTo.name: Watch and listen
howTo.text: Follow the sequence of lights and sounds.

howTo.name: Repeat it
howTo.text: Tap the pads in the same order. If you are right, the sequence grows by one.

howTo.name: Go for a high score
howTo.text: One mistake ends the game. Your best level is saved.

faq.question: How do I play Simon?
faq.answer: Watch the pattern, then repeat it by tapping the pads in the same order. Each round adds one more step.

faq.question: Do I need sound?
faq.answer: Sound helps you remember the pattern, but the lights work without it.

faq.question: What is a good score?
faq.answer: Reaching level 8 or 9 is good for most people. Above 12 is very good.

faq.question: Does it train memory?
faq.answer: It exercises short-term sequence memory and attention. It is a fun brain exercise, not a treatment.

faq.question: Is my best score saved?
faq.answer: Yes, in your browser on this device only.

faq.question: Can I play on a phone?
faq.answer: Yes. The pads are large touch targets.

faq.question: Does the time to memorise change?

faq.question: Does it follow the order of operations?
faq.answer: Yes. Brackets first, then powers and roots, then multiplication and division, then addition and subtraction. So 2+3×4 gives 14, and −2² gives −4.

faq.question: How do I switch between degrees and radians?
faq.answer: Tap the DEG or RAD label above the display. In degrees sin(30) = 0.5; in radians it is about −0.988.

faq.question: What does 2nd do?
faq.answer: It switches the function keys: sin, cos and tan become their inverses, ln becomes eˣ, log becomes 10ˣ, √ becomes a cube root, x² becomes x³, xʸ becomes a y-th root and n! becomes nCr.

faq.question: Is my history saved?

faq.question: Why does 0.1 + 0.2 show 0.3?
faq.answer: The calculator tidies the tiny rounding errors that computers make with decimals, and shows up to 12 significant digits.

faq.question: Which functions are supported?
faq.answer: Trigonometric and hyperbolic functions, their inverses, log, ln, square and cube roots, any power and root, factorial, permutations and combinations, absolute value, percent, π and e.

faq.question: Why are there gaps in my graph?
faq.answer: The graph is not drawn where the function is undefined, for example 1/x at x = 0 or sqrt(x) for negative x.

faq.question: Radians or degrees?
faq.answer: Graphs use radians by default. Tap RAD/DEG to switch the angle mode for sin, cos and tan.

faq.question: How accurate is the graph?
faq.answer: It is calculated at every pixel across the screen. Zoom in to look closely at a small area.

faq.question: When can two matrices be multiplied?
faq.answer: The number of columns of A must equal the number of rows of B. The result has the rows of A and the columns of B.

faq.question: What is a determinant?
faq.answer: A single number found from a square matrix. If it is 0 the matrix has no inverse.

faq.question: Why does it say there is no inverse?
faq.answer: Only square matrices with a determinant that is not 0 can be inverted.

faq.question: What is the trace?
faq.answer: The sum of the numbers on the main diagonal of a square matrix.

faq.question: How big can the matrices be?
faq.answer: Up to 4 by 4, which covers most homework and exam questions.

faq.question: What is the quadratic formula?
faq.answer: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a. The part under the root, b² − 4ac, is called the discriminant.

faq.question: What does the discriminant tell me?
faq.answer: If it is positive there are two different real roots, if it is zero there is one repeated root, and if it is negative the roots are complex numbers.

faq.question: What are complex roots?
faq.answer: Solutions involving i, the square root of −1. They appear in pairs like −1 + 2i and −1 − 2i.

faq.question: Why can't a be 0?
faq.answer: Then the equation is linear, not quadratic, so the formula does not apply.

faq.question: What is the vertex?
faq.answer: The turning point of the parabola. Its x-value is −b/2a and it lies on the axis of symmetry.

faq.question: Is the answer exact?
faq.answer: Results are shown with up to 12 significant digits, using a numerically stable method for large coefficients.

howTo.text: Choose HEX, DEC, OCT or BIN. Keys that don't belong to the base are disabled.

faq.question: How do I convert hex to decimal?
faq.answer: Pick HEX, type the number, then look at the DEC line (or tap DEC). All bases update together.

faq.question: What does the word size do?
faq.answer: It sets how many bits a number has. Results wrap around within that size, using two's complement for negative numbers.

faq.question: What are AND, OR and XOR?
faq.answer: Bitwise operators that compare each bit: AND is 1 only if both are 1, OR is 1 if either is 1, and XOR is 1 if exactly one is 1.

faq.question: What do << and >> do?
faq.answer: Shift the bits left or right, which multiplies or divides by powers of two.

faq.question: How are negative numbers shown?
faq.answer: In decimal they have a minus sign. In hex, octal and binary they appear in two's complement for the chosen word size.

faq.question: Can it handle 64-bit values?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses big integers, so 64-bit numbers are exact.

faq.question: Does it work offline?
faq.answer: Yes. Everything runs in your browser.

faq.question: What is the difference between sample and population?
faq.answer: Use sample when your numbers are only part of a larger group; it divides by n − 1. Use population when you have every value; it divides by n.

faq.question: How is the median found?
faq.answer: Sort the numbers and take the middle one, or the average of the two middle ones if there is an even count.

faq.question: What if there is no mode?
faq.answer: If every number appears once there is no mode, and it shows none.

faq.question: How are quartiles calculated?
faq.answer: With linear interpolation between the closest values. Different textbooks use slightly different methods.

faq.question: What counts as an outlier?
faq.answer: A value more than 1.5 times the interquartile range below Q1 or above Q3.

faq.question: How many numbers can I enter?
faq.answer: Thousands. Everything is calculated instantly in your browser.

faq.question: Is my data saved?

faq.question: What is the GCD?
faq.answer: The largest number that divides all your numbers exactly. It is also called the HCF (highest common factor).

faq.question: What is the LCM?
faq.answer: The smallest number that is a multiple of all your numbers. It is useful for adding fractions with different denominators.

faq.question: What is Euclid's algorithm?
faq.answer: Repeatedly divide the larger number by the smaller and keep the remainder until it is 0. The last non-zero remainder is the GCD.

faq.question: How does prime factorization work?
faq.answer: Every whole number above 1 is a product of primes. For example, 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5.

faq.question: What does coprime mean?
faq.answer: Two numbers whose GCD is 1, meaning they share no factor other than 1.

faq.question: How large can the numbers be?
faq.answer: Up to one trillion, and up to twelve numbers at once.
